section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you drive much slower than the posted speed and impede traffic on a two-lane road, what should you do?
options: a:Continue driving slowly because it's safest.,b:Always keep the right-of-way.,c:Pull off the road and allow following vehicles to pass if traffic is backing up.
note: Driving significantly below the flow of traffic can be hazardous. On a two-lane road you may be required to pull off and let faster traffic pass.

question: When driving in fog, what should you do about speed and headlights?
options: a:Drive cautiously and reduce your speed.,b:Use your high beam headlights.,c:Keep your normal speed because visibility is unchanged.
note: Fog reduces visibility. Slow down, drive cautiously, and use low beams rather than high beams to improve visibility.

question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line indicate?
options: a:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the broken line.,b:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the solid line.,c:Passing on the left is permitted from either direction.
note: If the broken line is next to your lane, you may pass when safe; if the solid line is next to your lane, passing is prohibited.

question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light at an intersection mean?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Stop and wait for a green light.,c:Continue through normally without reducing speed.
note: A flashing yellow light warns drivers to slow down, watch for traffic, and proceed carefully.

question: What does an “End school zone” sign indicate?
options: a:The start of a reduced speed school zone.,b:The end of a reduced speed school zone.,c:A 20 mph speed limit begins here.
note: An 'End school zone' sign indicates the end of the reduced speed school zone; follow posted limits during the times indicated.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on a freeway, what is the correct action?
options: a:Go to the next exit and re-route.,b:Make a U-turn through the median.,c:Pull onto the shoulder and back up to the exit.
note: If you miss an exit, continue to the next exit; do not stop, back up, or cross the median on a freeway.

question: When traveling with small children in a vehicle, what is the safest practice?
options: a:Hold them securely by hand.,b:Ensure they are properly restrained in child seats or seat belts.,c:Allow them to stand in the back if supervised.
note: Children must be properly restrained in child safety seats or seat belts; holding a child in your arms is unsafe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do before passing another vehicle?
options: a:Check mirrors and blind spots, signal, and re-enter the lane when safe.,b:Honk three times before passing.,c:Return to your lane within 10 feet of the passed vehicle.
note: Before passing, check mirrors and blind spots, use your turn signal, and only return to the lane when you can see the passed vehicle's front in your rearview mirror.

question: What is a safe technique for negotiating a curve?
options: a:Increase speed entering the curve and slow on exit.,b:Slow down before entering and gradually accelerate as you exit.,c:Maintain the same speed throughout the entire curve.
note: Slow down before a curve to maintain control; accelerate gradually as you exit the curve.

question: Two solid white lines across a lane mark the boundaries of what, and how should you respond to pedestrians there?
options: a:They mark a crosswalk; you must yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk.,b:They mark a bicycle lane; vehicles have the right-of-way.,c:They mark a no-passing zone for vehicles only.
note: Two solid white lines often indicate a crosswalk; pedestrians in a crosswalk must be given the right-of-way.

question: At night, which road user is hardest to see?
options: a:Road signs.,b:Pedestrians.,c:Other motorists.
note: Pedestrians are the hardest to see at night compared with signs or other vehicles; use extra caution and headlights.

question: If a police officer stops you for a violation or equipment check, which document are you required to present?
options: a:Proof of registration.,b:Your driver license.,c:Proof of insurance.
note: When stopped, drivers must be able to produce their driver license, vehicle registration, and proof of insurance upon request.

question: When is it appropriate to use your horn?
options: a:When you have lost control and need to warn others.,b:When overtaking another car.,c:To get a slow driver to move out of the lane.
note: Use your horn to warn others of immediate danger (for example if you lose control); avoid unnecessary or aggressive horn use.

question: Regulatory signs are normally which color and must be obeyed?
options: a:White,b:Blue,c:Green
note: Regulatory signs are typically white with black or red markings and indicate traffic laws or regulations that drivers are required to follow.

question: If you notice other drivers acting or reacting in anger, what should you do?
options: a:Don’t make eye contact with them.,b:React with hand gestures.,c:Distance yourself from the situation and avoid provoking them.
note: Avoid engagement: slow down, move over, avoid eye contact and gestures, and distance yourself to reduce the chance of escalation.

question: When approaching railroad crossing signals that are flashing, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down and look for a train.,b:Stop and look for a train, staying at least 15 feet from the rail if signals are warning.,c:Look, then speed up quickly to beat the train.
note: If crossing signals are flashing or gates are down, stop no closer than 15 feet from the nearest rail and wait until it's safe to cross.

question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, what must drivers do?
options: a:Follow the crossing guard's directions.,b:Follow the actions of surrounding traffic regardless of the guard's signals.,c:Assume the crossing guard has no authority to direct traffic.
note: Obey crossing guards and reduce speed as directed in school zones; their directions take precedence for pedestrian safety.

question: When passing a vehicle that has just parked at the curb, what should you assume?
options: a:The parked vehicle may open a door as you pass.,b:It is safe to speed up when passing.,c:You must slam on your brakes.
note: Assume the occupant of a parked vehicle may open the door; take extra caution when passing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering interstate traffic from an acceleration ramp, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:You should yield to drivers already on the interstate.,b:You have the right-of-way over interstate traffic.,c:You may force your way into traffic when needed.
note: When merging onto an interstate, yield to vehicles already on the roadway and merge when it is safe to do so.

question: Which of the following is true about work zones?
options: a:They may be stationary or moving and require reduced speed and extra attention.,b:They are marked with black and white signs only.,c:Drivers do not need to change behavior in a work zone.
note: Work zones can be stationary or involve moving operations (e.g., mowing, striping). They are marked with orange signs; slow down and be extra cautious.

question: When driving in fog, which lights should you use?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Parking lights only.,d:Four-way flashers only.
note: Use low beam headlights and fog lights if equipped. High beams reflect off the fog and worsen visibility.

question: What should you do before making a turn?
options: a:Use your turn signal a few seconds ahead of the turn.,b:Turn the wheel immediately without signaling.,c:Increase your speed.
note: Signal three to four seconds in advance (or appropriate distance) before turning to inform other road users of your intent.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do when preparing to change lanes?
options: a:Check your side and rearview mirrors and signal.,b:Not give any signals.,c:Quickly steer before checking mirrors.
note: Before changing lanes, check side and rearview mirrors, signal your intention, and glance over your shoulder to ensure the lane is clear.

question: When driving through a neighborhood or area where children are playing, what should you expect?
options: a:Children may run out into the street without looking.,b:Children will always stop at the curb before crossing.,c:Children will wait for an adult to cross.
note: Children may fail to judge traffic and can run into the street suddenly; reduce speed and be extra alert.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you pass your exit on the interstate, what should you do?
options: a:Continue to the next exit and re-enter the route back to your destination.,b:Make a sudden lane change to reach your exit.,c:Stop and back up to the exit.
note: Do not make sudden maneuvers or back up on the interstate; proceed to the next exit and return to your intended exit safely.

question: If your power steering fails while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Turn on your hazard lights and immediately turn off the ignition.,b:Work hard to steer, reduce your speed, drive to a safe area, and stop.,c:Honk your horn and turn off the ignition.
note: Power steering failure increases steering effort; slow down, steer carefully to a safe place, and stop.

question: If stopped at a multi-track railroad crossing, when may you proceed?
options: a:Only after you have a clear view down all tracks and no trains are approaching.,b:Immediately after the first train passes.,c:As soon as the gates rise on the nearest track.
note: When more than one track exists, wait until you can see clearly down all tracks and are sure no other trains are coming before proceeding.

question: If waiting in the intersection to complete a left turn, how should your wheels be positioned?
options: a:Keep your wheels straight while signaling.,b:Keep your wheels turned left to enter quickly.,c:Flash headlights to get drivers to let you through.
note: When waiting to turn left, signal and keep the wheels straight; being hit from behind is less likely to push you into oncoming traffic.

question: When must you stop at a railroad crossing?
options: a:When flashing red signals and gates are operating.,b:Only when you see a train.,c:Never stop if the tracks appear clear.
note: Stop at railroad crossings when warning lights flash or gates are down, or when a flagger or stop sign directs you to stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a flashing red light on a traffic signal signify?
options: a:You must come to a complete stop like at a stop sign.,b:The traffic signal is malfunctioning and you may drive normally.,c:You may slow down and go without stopping.
note: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign: stop, yield, then proceed when safe.

question: Approaching a railroad crossing without signals, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down and be prepared to stop if a train is approaching.,b:Always stop completely regardless of visibility.,c:Assume there will be a signal and proceed normally.
note: At unmarked crossings, slow down, look and listen for trains, and be prepared to stop if necessary; never assume the crossing is protected.

question: If your accelerator becomes stuck while driving, what is the correct action?
options: a:Shift into neutral and apply steady braking.,b:Shift to park immediately.,c:Try to pull the accelerator up while driving.,d:Turn off the headlights and coast to a stop.
note: Keep your eyes on the road, shift to neutral, apply steady pressure to the brakes, pull off the road when safe, and then turn off the engine.

question: On slippery roads you should:
options: a:Slow down.,b:Drive the posted speed but with caution.,c:Drive more quickly to get through the area.,d:Turn on hazard lights and maintain speed.
note: Slow down at the first sign of rain, snow, or sleet; on slippery surfaces you may need to drive more slowly than the posted limit for safety.

question: Which describes a good defensive driver?
options: a:Always drives slowly.,b:Anticipates and watches for actions by other drivers.,c:Maintains a single constant speed at all times.
note: A defensive driver watches for the actions of others and anticipates potential problems rather than relying on fixed speed.

question: When driving in fog, which headlights should you use?
options: a:Use your parking lights.,b:Use your high beams.,c:Use your low beam headlights.
note: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, or snow to reduce glare and maintain better visibility.

question: How should you handle being followed too closely by another vehicle?
options: a:Check traffic behind frequently and let them pass when safe.,b:Brake suddenly to warn them.,c:Increase your speed so they drop back.
note: Monitor the roadway behind you and either slow gradually or change lanes to let tailgaters pass; avoid sudden braking or speeding up.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are turning left onto a one-way street, into which lane should you turn?
options: a:The right lane.,b:The lane closest to your previous lane.,c:Either lane, depending on traffic.
note: Turn into the lane closest to the direction you came from—typically the lane nearest your original lane on the one-way street.

question: Which statement about passing motorcycles is true?
options: a:A passenger vehicle must change lanes completely when passing a motorcycle.,b:It is okay to follow motorcycles closely.,c:A motorcycle is entitled to the full lane width like other vehicles.
note: Motorcycles are entitled to the full width of a lane; be sure your vehicle is entirely in the left lane before passing on the left.

question: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is nearby, how should you respond?
options: a:Try to speed up to get out of the way.,b:Stop your vehicle immediately to block their path.,c:Make every effort to give them a clear path of travel, pulling to the side if safe.
note: When an emergency vehicle is approaching, move out of its path if possible—pull to the side and stop if it is safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A posted speed limit sign indicates:
options: a:The maximum safe driving speed under ideal road and weather conditions.,b:Only a recommended driving speed.,c:The exact speed you must travel to avoid a ticket.
note: Speed limit signs show the maximum legal speed under ideal conditions; adjust lower for poor weather or visibility.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you proceed through an intersection controlled by a stop sign with no stop line or crosswalk?
options: a:After slowing to check for cross traffic.,b:After coming to a complete stop before entering the intersection and ensuring it is safe.,c:After stopping at least 20 feet before the intersection.
note: If there is a stop sign but no marked line or crosswalk, stop before entering the intersection and go only when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which instruction takes precedence over the others: a steady red light, a police officer, or a stop sign?
options: a:A steady red light.,b:A stop sign.,c:A police officer directing traffic.
note: An authorized traffic officer's directions override signs, signals, and pavement markings.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When can you park or stop on the shoulder of a freeway?
options: a:If you turn on four-way flashers.,b:Only in an emergency.,c:If you need to check a map for directions.
note: Parking on the freeway shoulder is prohibited except in emergencies.

question: What shape is a stop sign?
options: a:Rectangle.,b:Octagon.,c:Circle.
note: Stop signs are uniquely octagonal (eight-sided) to indicate that drivers must come to a complete stop.

question: If you arrive at an accident scene, when should you stop?
options: a:Only if you are involved or if emergency help has not yet arrived.,b:Always stop and offer assistance regardless of circumstances.,c:Stop in the roadway to get a better view.
note: Do not stop to view the accident. Only stop if you are involved, can render aid safely, or if emergency help has not arrived and you can assist without creating hazards.

question: What is a common cause of many crashes?
options: a:Driving too fast for road conditions.,b:Consistently checking mirrors and blind spots.,c:Yielding the right-of-way too often.
note: Many crashes occur because drivers travel too fast for conditions; always adjust speed to road and weather.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a highway from an entrance ramp, you should generally:
options: a:Stop at the end of the ramp and wait for a big gap.,b:Accelerate to match the speed of traffic and merge when safe.,c:Enter well below the speed of traffic to be cautious.,d:Immediately move into the leftmost lane.
note: Use the acceleration lane to match the speed of traffic, signal, and merge into a safe opening in traffic.

question: When will you receive a point accumulation advisory letter?
options: a:When you accumulate four points in 12 months.,b:When you are fined for speeding.,c:When points are taken off your driving record.
note: If you accumulate a total of four points within 12 months, you will be sent a point accumulation advisory letter.

question: At night when another vehicle is approaching, how should your headlights be set?
options: a:On low beam.,b:On high beam.,c:Off (use parking lights).
note: Do not use high beams when approaching or following another vehicle; switch to low beams for safety.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering public traffic from a driveway or private road, who must yield?
options: a:The driver entering from the driveway should yield to traffic already on the public road.,b:The public traffic must always stop for you.,c:You may force your way into traffic if necessary.
note: Vehicles entering from driveways or private roads must yield to drivers already on the public road and merge safely when possible.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you proceed when approaching an intersection with a flashing yellow light?
options: a:Drive carefully through the intersection after slowing and scanning for hazards.,b:Stop and wait for the light to change.,c:Make a U-turn because the road is closed.
note: A flashing yellow light means slow down and proceed with caution; scan traffic in both directions before entering.

question: How can you avoid being in a truck or bus driver's blind spot?
options: a:Avoid driving alongside and do not tailgate them.,b:Never pass them under any circumstances.,c:Flash your lights at them.
note: Large vehicles have big blind spots; avoid lingering alongside them and never tailgate.

question: When it begins to rain while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down and turn on your headlights.,b:Drive at the posted maximum speed limit.,c:Speed up to get through the rain quickly.
note: Reduce speed when visibility is reduced by rain and turn on headlights; if visibility is severely limited, pull off safely.

question: What is defensive driving?
options: a:Following the vehicle ahead at a close distance.,b:Identifying dangerous driving situations and taking action to avoid accidents.,c:Defending yourself by getting ahead of poor drivers.
note: Defensive driving means anticipating hazards and acting to prevent conflicts and crashes.

question: If you are taking a non-prescription (over-the-counter) drug, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Read the label for warnings about driving.,b:Mix it with alcohol to see how it affects you.,c:Ignore the label and drive as usual.,d:Only drive if you feel fine.
note: Many over-the-counter medications can impair driving. Check labels for warnings and consult a doctor or pharmacist if unsure.

question: Why is a leaky exhaust system dangerous?
options: a:It increases air pollution.,b:It can cause carbon monoxide poisoning.,c:It may reduce engine performance.
note: An exhaust leak can allow carbon monoxide to enter the passenger compartment; repair any exhaust system leaks promptly to prevent poisoning.

question: Which statement about alcohol and driving is true?
options: a:Only a BAC above the legal limit will impair concentration.,b:Alcohol does not limit concentration, perception, or memory.,c:Even the smallest amount of alcohol can reduce concentration, perception, judgment, and memory.
note: Any alcohol can impair driving skills. No one can drink and drive safely; impairment begins with the first drink.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of these is NOT permitted while stopped in a travel lane?
options: a:Stopping to drop off passengers.,b:Stopping to look up an address.,c:Keeping moving until you can safely pull off the road.
note: You should not stop in a travel lane for any reason. Continue moving until you can safely pull off the roadway.

question: If someone has been drinking, what will help them sober up quickly?
options: a:Hot coffee.,b:Fresh air.,c:Time—only the passage of time will lessen alcohol's effects.
note: Only time allows the body to metabolize alcohol; coffee, fresh air, or exercise do not speed sobriety.

question: How does consuming alcohol while taking drugs affect you?
options: a:It reduces the effects of both.,b:It can increase the effects of both, making driving more dangerous.,c:It helps cure whatever illness you have.
note: Combining alcohol with drugs can magnify impairment and seriously increase crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you pass another vehicle based on lane markings between lanes moving the same direction?
options: a:When the dividing line is a broken white line.,b:When there is a solid yellow line.,c:When there is a double solid yellow line.
note: Broken white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and may be crossed to pass when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A red flashing traffic light has the same meaning as which sign?
options: a:A stop sign.,b:A solid red light.,c:A yield sign.
note: A flashing red traffic signal is treated like a stop sign: come to a full stop and proceed when safe.

question: When traveling to a place you don't know well, what should you do before you drive?
options: a:Only have a general idea where your destination is.,b:Plan your route ahead of time.,c:Rely solely on road signs to find your way.
note: Plan your trip in advance; don’t depend only on a vague idea or only on signs when going to an unfamiliar area.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you see a flashing red light at an intersection, what must you do?
options: a:Proceed with caution without stopping.,b:Come to a complete stop, then go when safe.,c:Slow down but you don’t have to stop.
note: A flashing red signal means you must stop, yield to other traffic and pedestrians, and proceed only when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When overtaking on a multilane highway, what should you do before beginning to pass?
options: a:Pass only on the right.,b:Watch for oncoming traffic.,c:Make sure the passing lane is clear and signal before changing lanes.
note: Always verify the passing lane is clear and use your turn signal before changing lanes to pass.

question: How does being distracted while driving usually affect your reactions to hazards?
options: a:It has no effect.,b:It generally slows your reaction to hazards.,c:It makes you react faster.
note: Distractions cause slower reactions to traffic and hazards and significantly increase crash risk.

question: Which situation most commonly causes “highway hypnosis” while driving?
options: a:Too much sleep the night before your trip.,b:Frequent rest stops.,c:Staring at the roadway for long periods and failing to actively scan.
note: 'Highway hypnosis' occurs when a driver stares straight ahead for long periods and stops actively scanning the road, increasing crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on an interstate, what should you do?
options: a:Continue to the next exit and safely turn around.,b:Stop on the shoulder and back up to the exit.,c:Make an immediate U-turn across lanes.
note: Do not back up or attempt a U-turn on the highway. Proceed to the next exit and re-route safely.

question: Approaching a railroad crossing with only a crossbuck and no gates or flashing lights, you should:
options: a:Proceed when you think it is clear.,b:Turn up the radio to listen for trains.,c:Approach with extreme caution and cross only when you know no train is coming.,d:Always wait for a flagger even if none is present.
note: Approach with extreme caution and cross only when you are certain no train is coming from either direction; obey flaggers if present.

question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light mean?
options: a:Merging traffic is ahead.,b:Proceed with caution.,c:Pedestrian crossing only.
note: A flashing yellow light warns drivers to proceed with caution through the intersection.

question: What is the purpose of a diamond-shaped road sign?
options: a:To warn of existing or possible hazards.,b:To indicate a public recreation area.,c:To mark school zones.
note: Diamond-shaped signs (usually yellow or orange) warn of conditions or hazards on or near the roadway.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If turning onto a multi-lane street, into which lane should you turn?
options: a:Into the lane closest to your previous lane.,b:Into the middle lane regardless of approach.,c:Into any lane and then change immediately.
note: When turning onto a street with more than one lane in your direction, turn into the lane closest to the one you came from.

question: Which of these is a common sign of a drunk driver?
options: a:Weaving between lanes.,b:Driving more slowly than normal traffic.,c:Making quick and sudden stops.
note: Common signs of impairment include weaving, speed variations, jerking movements, and sudden stops—any erratic driving suggests possible impairment.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A steady yellow traffic light at an intersection means you should:
options: a:Go.,b:Yield to other cars.,c:Slow down and prepare to stop.
note: A steady yellow warns that the light will soon turn red; slow down and be prepared to stop unless unsafe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You may legally pass another vehicle when:
options: a:Your lane is next to a solid yellow line and the passing lane is clear ahead.,b:On a hill or in a curve where visibility is limited.,c:The center line on your side of the roadway is a broken yellow line and it is safe to pass.,d:By driving onto the highway shoulder.
note: Only pass where pavement markings and conditions permit—do not pass on hills, curves, over solid lines, or on the shoulder.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What are the minimum and maximum speed limits on Missouri interstates under normal conditions?
options: a:40 mph minimum and 70 mph maximum.,b:40 mph minimum and 55 mph maximum.,c:30 mph minimum and 70 mph maximum.
note: On Missouri interstate highways the normal posted maximum is 70 mph and the minimum under normal conditions is 40 mph.

question: What does the abbreviation FACT stand for?
options: a:Failure to Appear in Court for Traffic violations.,b:Finance A Car Today.,c:Full Ambulance Cannot Turn.,d:Fear of Authority Causes Tension.
note: FACT means Failure to Appear in Court for Traffic violations. Failing to appear can lead to court action and license suspension.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do while driving on major highways to avoid highway hypnosis and be ready for hazards?
options: a:Keep your eyes moving.,b:Stay alert.,c:Be ready to react to road hazards.
note: Keep your eyes moving and stay attentive to prevent zoning out and to detect hazards early on highways.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection where two vehicles arrive simultaneously, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The car that sounds its horn first.,b:The car approaching from the right.,c:The car approaching from the left.
note: If no signs or signals control the intersection, yield to the vehicle approaching from your right.

question: A double solid yellow centerline indicates what?
options: a:Single broken yellow.,b:Passing is not permitted from either direction.,c:Combination solid and broken yellow.
note: Double solid yellow lines separate two-way traffic and indicate that passing from either direction is prohibited.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a steady green traffic light at an intersection allow you to do?
options: a:Must stop and check for oncoming traffic before proceeding.,b:May drive through the intersection if the way is clear.,c:Must slow down and prepare to stop.
note: A steady green light permits you to go through the intersection when the way is clear; yield to pedestrians and other traffic when turning.

question: Which factors influence the effects of alcohol on a person?
options: a:The amount of food in the stomach,b:The individual's body weight,c:The time between drinks,d:All of the above
note: BAC depends on how much alcohol you drink, how long between drinks, your weight, and whether you've eaten. Food slows absorption but cannot prevent impairment.

question: Where are roads most likely to freeze quickly?
options: a:In shaded areas such as those by trees or buildings.,b:On straight, open sections of road.,c:Where the sun hits directly.
note: Shaded portions of the roadway freeze sooner and remain icy longer than areas exposed to the sun; exercise extra caution there in cold weather.

question: If your wheels drop off the pavement onto the shoulder, how should you return to the pavement?
options: a:Slow down and very carefully turn back onto the pavement.,b:Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the pavement.,c:Stop your car on the edge of the road.
note: Reduce speed without braking abruptly, then carefully steer back onto the pavement when it's safe to do so.

question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?
options: a:Bad weather.,b:New drivers.,c:Human error.
note: Most crashes result from human error—mistakes in observation, judgment, or vehicle handling.

question: Compared to smaller vehicles, larger vehicles generally have what regarding blind spots?
options: a:Larger blind spots.,b:Smaller blind spots.,c:No blind spots at all.
note: The larger the vehicle, the larger its blind spots. Be especially cautious around trucks and large SUVs.

question: Does drinking coffee lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Yes, it decreases BAC.,b:No, it has no effect on BAC.,c:Yes, it cancels the alcohol's effects.
note: Coffee may make you more alert but does not reduce your blood alcohol concentration or sober you up.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To pass a slower vehicle on a two-lane, two-way road, what is required?
options: a:You must temporarily use the lane for oncoming traffic and ensure it is safe to pass.,b:You may not cross the centerline under any circumstance.,c:Flash your headlights at oncoming traffic to warn them.
note: Passing on a two-lane two-way road requires using the opposing lane; only pass when you can do so safely and legally.

question: If an approaching train is close enough to be a danger, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Not cross the tracks until the train has passed completely.,c:Cross the tracks at your own risk if you are in a hurry.
note: If a train is close enough to be dangerous, you must not cross the tracks until it has passed, even if signals are not working.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do before changing lanes?
options: a:Check your side-view mirror only.,b:Check your rearview mirror only.,c:Check side and rearview mirrors and glance over your shoulder to check the blind spot.
note: Before changing lanes, check mirrors for traffic and look over your shoulder in the direction of your move to verify the blind spot is clear.

question: If an oncoming vehicle has blinding headlights, what should you do?
options: a:Look directly at the headlights until they dim.,b:Look toward the right edge of the road until the vehicle has passed.,c:Flash your high beams to signal them to dim.
note: Look away from the high beams and toward the right side of the road until the oncoming car has passed to avoid being blinded.

question: How should you respond when approaching a flashing yellow traffic signal?
options: a:Increase your speed.,b:Come to a complete stop.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.
note: A flashing yellow light warns of a hazard; slow down and proceed with caution.

question: When roads may be slippery, what should you avoid?
options: a:Using cruise control and making sudden speed or steering changes.,b:Reducing your speed.,c:Driving more cautiously than normal.
note: On slippery roads, avoid cruise control and any sudden changes in speed or direction; reduce speed and increase following distance.

question: If you are upset, nervous, or crying, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Start driving and let emotions settle.,b:Take time to calm down and focus on driving before you start.,c:Drive faster to get it over with.
note: Strong emotions can impair driving; take time to calm and focus before getting behind the wheel.

question: What does a red circle with a diagonal slash on a regulatory sign mean?
options: a:The indicated action is forbidden.,b:Drivers must come to a complete stop.,c:Some drivers should yield to others.
note: A red circle with a slash over a black symbol on a white regulatory sign means the specified action is prohibited.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a heavy truck from behind on an uphill grade, what should you expect?
options: a:The truck may be traveling at a speed slower than the posted limit.,b:You may not be able to safely pass the truck because of limited visibility or grade.,c:The truck will always signal you to pass.
note: Large vehicles often travel slower uphill; on hills with limited sight distance it may be unsafe or illegal to attempt a pass.

question: How should you respond to an aggressive driver?
options: a:Retaliate by tailgating them.,b:Cut them off to slow them down.,c:Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
note: Keep calm, avoid confrontation, and allow aggressive drivers to pass to reduce the risk of escalation.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a right turn on a green light, what must you do?
options: a:Yield to pedestrians and other traffic as required.,b:Maintain normal speed without stopping.,c:Stop and wait for a police officer to direct you.
note: When turning on a green, you must still yield to pedestrians and other traffic in the intersection unless signs prohibit the turn.

question: When an emergency vehicle is using its lights and/or siren, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down and stay in your lane.,b:Pull to the right curb and stop, yielding a clear path.,c:Keep driving in your lane and ignore it.
note: You must pull over to the curb or side of the road and stop to give emergency vehicles a clear path when safe to do so.

question: What is required regarding visibility of license plates and plate frames in Missouri?
options: a:A frame may cover the word \"\"Missouri\"\" on the plate.,b:Plate frames should not cover any portion of the plate's information.,c:A frame may cover the month and year registration stickers.
note: License plates must be fully visible and not obscured by frames or covers so law enforcement can inspect them easily.

question: What greatly increases stopping distances and crash severity?
options: a:Night driving.,b:High speeds.,c:Slow speeds.
note: Higher speeds increase stopping distances and collision severity; the faster you go, the greater the impact energy.

question: If you are involved in a crash, what should you do first?
options: a:Stop at once.,b:Leave the scene if damage is only minor.,c:Only call the police if someone is injured.,d:Move injured people immediately without checking injuries.
note: Stop immediately, render aid if it is safe, call the police and ambulance if needed, exchange information, and avoid moving injured persons unless necessary.

question: About how far might a fully loaded tractor-trailer traveling 55 mph need to stop?
options: a:50 feet,b:125 feet,c:Up to 400 feet.
note: A fully loaded tractor-trailer can take nearly 400 feet to stop at 55 mph—much longer than a passenger car.

question: What is the correct method for backing a vehicle?
options: a:Turn your head and look through the rear window while backing, not relying solely on mirrors.,b:Rely only on your mirrors.,c:Open your door and step out to check behind you.
note: Before backing, check behind the vehicle; while backing, turn your head and look through the rear window rather than relying solely on mirrors.

question: On roads without sidewalks, which side should pedestrians walk on?
options: a:The side that faces oncoming traffic.,b:The same side that traffic travels on.,c:The side with lighter traffic.
note: Pedestrians should walk on the side of the road facing oncoming traffic so they can see and react to approaching vehicles.

question: If you arrive at your car feeling angry after an incident, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Play loud music so you won’t think about it.,b:Drive fast on the interstate to let off steam.,c:Take a few minutes to cool off before you begin driving home.
note: Do not drive while emotionally upset. Take a few minutes to cool down before driving to avoid poor judgment and dangerous behavior.

question: If you hear a siren behind you while driving, you should:
options: a:Speed up to get out of the way.,b:Pull over to the right and stop.,c:Stop immediately where you are.,d:Turn on your hazard lights and continue driving.
note: Create a clear path for the emergency vehicle by safely pulling over to the right and stopping; in heavy traffic, move slowly until you can get out of the way.

question: What primarily affects your ability to stop your vehicle safely?
options: a:The condition of the road and roadway surfaces.,b:The time of day.,c:Signal lights alone.
note: Road conditions (wet, icy, gravel) greatly affect stopping distance; reduce speed accordingly to maintain control.

question: When making a turn, how should you adjust your speed?
options: a:Increase your speed.,b:Maintain the same speed as before.,c:Reduce or otherwise adjust your speed to maintain control.
note: Reduce speed when turning to keep control of your vehicle, stay in your lane, and respond to unexpected situations.

question: What is the correct way to use a freeway exit ramp?
options: a:Do not slow down until you have moved onto the exit ramp, then decelerate.,b:Slow down before entering the exit ramp.,c:Keep speed constant once on the exit ramp.
note: On freeway exits, maintain freeway speed until you are on the exit ramp, then slow as needed in the deceleration lane.

question: How can you avoid having to make sudden emergency stops when driving in traffic?
options: a:Drive in the right lane only.,b:Look ahead and maintain a safe following distance.,c:Honk your horn to alert others of your presence.
note: Keeping a safe following distance and anticipating traffic ahead reduces the need for sudden emergency braking.

question: On a roadway divided by double solid yellow lines, when are you allowed to cross them?
options: a:Only to make a left turn into or from an alley, private road, or driveway.,b:To pass slower vehicles if no oncoming traffic is present.,c:Never under any circumstances.
note: Double solid yellow lines separate opposing traffic and generally prohibit passing; you may cross them only to make a left turn into or from an alley, private road, or driveway.

question: You may cross double solid yellow lines to:
options: a:Pass a slow-moving vehicle.,b:Turn into a driveway or make a left turn where it is permitted.,c:Change lanes at any time.,d:Use the shoulder to pass.
note: Double solid yellow lines prohibit passing and lane changes; you may cross them to turn into or out of driveways or to make permitted left turns.

question: Which statement about littering from a vehicle is true?
options: a:Littering is illegal and can lead to fines or jail time.,b:Littering is not regulated.,c:Littering rarely causes accidents.
note: Littering is against the law and can be dangerous—thrown items may cause crashes. Fines and jail time are possible upon conviction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes from the right lane into the left on a multilane highway, what should you check?
options: a:Only your rearview mirror for traffic behind you.,b:Over your left shoulder to check your blind spot before changing lanes.,c:Turn on your directional signal and immediately swerve left.
note: Check mirrors and also look over your left shoulder to confirm the blind spot is clear before you change lanes; always signal your intent.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: From which lane should you start a left turn on a multilane one-way street?
options: a:The left lane.,b:The right lane.,c:The middle of the intersection.
note: To turn left from a multilane one-way street, begin the turn from the leftmost lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must you do when you approach an intersection with a flashing red light?
options: a:Stop completely, then proceed when the way is clear.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution without stopping.,c:Wait until the light turns green before moving.
note: A flashing red light requires a full stop; proceed only when it is safe to do so, similar to a stop sign.

question: What does a red arrow signal require drivers to do?
options: a:Stop and remain stopped until a green light or green arrow is displayed.,b:Slow and proceed with caution.,c:Stop and then proceed when clear even if the arrow remains red.
note: A red arrow means you must stop and remain stopped until a green signal or green arrow permits movement in that direction.

question: What actions should you take when approaching a railroad crossing?
options: a:Slow down, look, and be prepared to stop.,b:Speed up to clear the tracks quickly.,c:Assume the crossing is clear unless gates are down.
note: When approaching a railroad crossing, slow down, look both ways, and be ready to stop; stop 15–50 feet before tracks if signals or gates indicate.

question: If a pedestrian begins crossing in front of you, what is the correct action?
options: a:Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrian.,b:Flash your lights.,c:Slow down and be prepared to stop.
note: Always slow and be ready to stop for pedestrians, yielding the right-of-way to those in crosswalks.

question: When is it appropriate to use your horn?
options: a:To warn a child who is about to run into the street.,b:When traveling through an intersection.,c:While passing a bicyclist to be polite.
note: Use your horn as a warning in dangerous situations, such as if a child is about to run into the roadway.

question: How should you check your blind spot before changing lanes?
options: a:Look into the left side mirror.,b:Look into the rearview mirror.,c:Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.
note: A quick shoulder check in the direction you plan to move reveals vehicles or cyclists in your blind spot.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an intersection controlled by a yield sign, what must you do?
options: a:Always come to a complete stop even if no traffic is present.,b:Slow down and yield to traffic in or approaching the roadway you are entering.,c:Yield only to traffic on the right.
note: A yield sign means you must slow and yield the right-of-way to traffic in the intersection or road you are entering.

question: Which conditions can impair a person's ability to drive safely?
options: a:A lack of sleep.,b:Alcohol.,c:Both sleep deprivation and alcohol can impair driving.
note: Driving ability can be impaired by alcohol, legal and illegal drugs, and being drowsy—any of these reduce safe driving ability.

question: When should you increase your following distance?
options: a:When driving behind a large vehicle that blocks your vision.,b:When exiting an expressway only.,c:Only when following a motorcycle.
note: Increase following distance when a large vehicle blocks your view, in bad weather, heavy traffic, when exiting an expressway, and when following motorcycles or bicycles.

question: What do two solid yellow lines down the center of the road indicate?
options: a:Passing is allowed for drivers from both directions.,b:Passing is not allowed.,c:Passing is allowed when going over a hill.
note: Two solid yellow lines mean passing from either direction is prohibited because of reduced visibility or other hazards.

question: What can happen if you drink alcohol while taking prescription or over-the-counter medicine?
options: a:The combination may multiply the impairing effects of either the alcohol or the medicine.,b:The medicine negates the alcohol's effects.,c:Alcohol helps the medicine work better.
note: Combining alcohol with medications can intensify impairment and may have dangerous or unpredictable effects.

question: Which of the following is a restriction for an intermediate driver's license?
options: a:No passengers at any time.,b:Driving curfew between 1:00 a.m. and 5:00 a.m. except for school/activity/job or emergency.,c:No seat belt required for the driver.
note: Intermediate license holders may not drive alone between 1:00 a.m. and 5:00 a.m. except for specified reasons; seat belts are required for all occupants.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you reach an intersection that is blocked with traffic ahead, what should you do?
options: a:Get as close as possible to the car in front of you.,b:Stay out of the intersection until you can pass through.,c:Go slowly until the traffic ahead moves.
note: Do not enter an intersection unless you can fully clear it; blocking the intersection is illegal and unsafe.

question: What do highway pavement markings and other roadway markings provide for drivers?
options: a:Are usually not important.,b:Provide information for drivers.,c:Are only found in construction zones.
note: Pavement markings guide lane positioning, passing zones, and warn about upcoming roadway conditions.

question: What usually causes hydroplaning?
options: a:Driving at excessive speeds on wet roads causing tires to ride on a film of water.,b:Excessive stops.,c:Sudden turns at low speed.
note: Hydroplaning occurs when tires cannot clear water at higher speeds and begin to ride on a film of water.

question: Which device increases crash risk when used while driving:
options: a:A CD player.,b:A cell phone.,c:A radio.
note: Using a cell phone (including hands-free) is a serious distraction and increases crash risk.

question: Which driving practice helps avoid crashes on icy or snowy roads?
options: a:Reduce speed and increase following distance.,b:Add extra weight to the vehicle to improve traction.,c:Get off the highway immediately.
note: Slowing down and increasing following distance are the most important ways to reduce crash risk on snow- or ice-covered roads.

question: What do orange-colored traffic signs typically indicate?
options: a:Work zones or construction ahead.,b:School zones.,c:Regulatory requirements like stop or speed limits.
note: Orange signs are used for highway work zones and warn drivers of construction or maintenance on or near the road.

question: When you are approached by an emergency vehicle using lights and/or siren, you must immediately:
options: a:Pull to the right and turn on your vehicle's four-way flashers.,b:Pull to the right and slow down.,c:Pull to the right and stop.
note: If an emergency vehicle is approaching with warning devices, pull to the right side of the road and stop until it passes.

question: A solid white edge line on the right that slants left indicates what ahead?
options: a:The road is narrowing ahead.,b:An intersection is ahead.,c:A left turn is required ahead.
note: An edge line angling toward the center of the road signals that the road will be narrower ahead.

question: If you are involved in a serious motor vehicle crash, what should you first do?
options: a:Stop at or near the scene.,b:Call the police immediately without stopping.,c:Drive home and report it later.
note: If involved in a crash stop and move your vehicle out of traffic if possible. Call 911 if there are injuries; you must report crashes with injury, death, or significant property damage.

question: If there are two railroad tracks side by side, what should you do after one train passes?
options: a:Begin to cross immediately since one train has passed.,b:Always stop before crossing even if no train is visible.,c:Look for another train on the other track before proceeding.,d:Speed up to clear the tracks quickly.
note: Watch for a second train on the adjacent track; do not cross until you are sure no train is approaching on either track.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you signal before passing another vehicle?
options: a:Early enough for others to know your intention before you change lanes.,b:Only after you begin the lane change.,c:Only if other traffic is present.
note: Signal early enough that other drivers understand your intentions before you start the passing maneuver.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement about speed is true?
options: a:Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.,b:Speeding is never dangerous if you are a skilled driver.,c:Speed does not affect crash severity.
note: Both excessive speed and driving too slowly for conditions can be hazardous; higher speeds increase the chance of severe or fatal crashes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following is correct when passing another vehicle?
options: a:Signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes and ensure no oncoming traffic.,b:Use mirrors and look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot when passing to the left.,c:Wait until you can see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror before returning to your lane.,d:All of the above
note: When passing, signal early, check mirrors and blind spots, and return to your lane only when you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.

question: If an oncoming vehicle is in your lane headed straight at you, what should you do first?
options: a:Blow your horn, steer right, and accelerate.,b:Blow your horn, steer left, and brake.,c:Blow your horn, steer right, and brake.
note: Honk to warn the other driver, try to escape to the right, and brake firmly and steadily if necessary; swerving left risks a head-on crash.

question: What does a flashing yellow traffic signal signify?
options: a:Proceed with caution and slow down.,b:Stop and wait for a green light.,c:Speed up to cross quickly.
note: A flashing yellow light warns drivers to slow down and proceed through the intersection with caution.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a traffic light turns green, what is required before you proceed?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and any traffic still in the intersection.,b:Accelerate as fast as possible to clear the intersection.,c:Back up slowly if needed.
note: A green light allows you to go, but you must first yield to pedestrians and traffic still in the intersection.

question: Where is it legal to consume alcoholic beverages inside a vehicle on a public road?
options: a:It is not legal to consume or possess an alcoholic beverage on a public road.,b:Only if you are a passenger in the back seat.,c:Only in the bed of a pickup truck.
note: Missouri law prohibits consumption or possession of alcoholic beverages on public roadways and open containers in areas normally occupied by driver or passengers.

question: On a two-lane road without bicycle lanes, how should you pass a bicyclist going in the same direction?
options: a:Slow down and wait until no oncoming traffic is present, then pass with sufficient space.,b:Blow your horn and pass closely but quickly.,c:Never pass until you reach a traffic signal or stop sign.
note: Pass bicyclists as you would other vehicles but leave adequate space (at least 3 feet, more on higher-speed roads) and do so only when it is safe.

question: Is it permissible to drive around or under a crossing gate that is being lowered or raised?
options: a:If your vehicle can do so without damaging the gate.,b:If an approaching train is not too close.,c:No — do not drive around or under a moving gate.
note: Flashing lights or moving/ lowered gates mean stop. Never go around or under a gate while it is moving.

question: If you drive while intoxicated and cause injury or death to another person, what are possible consequences?
options: a:You will only have to pay a fine.,b:You will only lose your license.,c:You may face jail time, fines, and license loss.
note: Causing serious injury or death while intoxicated can result in prison, substantial fines, and long-term loss of driving privileges.

question: If you are in another driver's blind spot, what should you do?
options: a:Keep a steady pace.,b:Move forward or drop back so the other driver can see you.,c:Stay in the driver's blind spot.
note: Do not remain in another vehicle's blind spot; move forward or fall back so the driver can see you in their mirrors.

question: What does a steady yellow traffic signal mean?
options: a:The traffic signal is changing from green to red.,b:You should slam on your brakes immediately.,c:You should increase your speed to clear the intersection.
note: A steady yellow indicates the light is about to turn red—slow down and stop if you can do so safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If waiting to turn left and opposing traffic blocks your view, what is the correct action?
options: a:Accelerate rapidly when the first lane is clear.,b:Wait until you can see all the lanes you must cross before making the turn.,c:Rely on an oncoming driver to wave you through.
note: Do not begin a left turn until you can see all lanes you need to cross and are sure you can complete the turn safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a narrow road meeting an oncoming vehicle, what must you allow the other vehicle?
options: a:Demand the other vehicle pull over to make room.,b:Pull completely off the road and stop.,c:Allow the oncoming vehicle at least one-half of the main-traveled portion of the road.
note: On narrow roads both drivers should leave at least half the main-traveled surface to allow safe passage.

question: What is the only effective way to reduce your BAC?
options: a:Drink coffee.,b:Exercise.,c:Allow your body time to metabolize the alcohol.
note: Only the passage of time reduces BAC; coffee, exercise, or cold showers do not lower blood alcohol content.

question: Which actions help prevent hydroplaning?
options: a:Keep tires with good tread and proper inflation and reduce speed in rain.,b:Increase speed to cut through the water.,c:Ignore tire condition if roads look clear.
note: Good tread, correct tire pressure, and reduced speed in wet conditions all lower the chance of hydroplaning.

question: When approaching railroad tracks, what should you do?
options: a:Try to drive around a lowered gate.,b:Look, listen, slow down, and be prepared to stop.,c:Speed up to cross before the gate is lowered.
note: Approach railroad crossings prepared to stop; look and listen for trains and obey any signals or gates.

question: When driving near a motorcycle, what should you allow the rider to use?
options: a:Drive on the shoulder beside the motorcycle.,b:Allow the motorcycle to use a complete lane.,c:Allow the motorcycle to use only half of a lane.
note: A motorcycle is a full-size vehicle with the same roadway privileges as other vehicles. Give motorcyclists a full lane so they have room to maneuver safely.

question: Where are stop lines (solid white lines) painted on the roadway?
options: a:In curves and on hills.,b:Next to churches and schools.,c:At intersections and pedestrian crosswalks.
note: Stop lines mark exactly where drivers must stop for signs or signals and are painted across lanes at intersections and crosswalks.

question: When should you look over your shoulder to check a blind spot?
options: a:When pulling toward or away from a curb.,b:When turning left or right.,c:When changing lanes.
note: Always glance over your shoulder to check blind spots whenever you change lanes or move laterally in traffic.

question: Must traffic signs and pavement markings be obeyed?
options: a:Yes, they must always be obeyed.,b:No, they are only suggestions.,c:Only when other traffic is present.
note: Traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings regulate traffic flow and must be obeyed for lawful and safe driving.

question: How does driving faster affect tire performance on a wet roadway?
options: a:The faster you drive, the less effective your tires become at clearing water.,b:Water does not affect cars with good tires.,c:Deep water is less dangerous than shallow water.
note: As speed increases on wet roads, tires become less effective at clearing water and hydroplaning risk rises.

question: When is horn use appropriate in emergency situations?
options: a:To warn others if you have lost control of your vehicle.,b:To express anger at another driver.,c:To greet pedestrians.
note: The horn should be used to alert others to immediate danger (for example, if you lose control); avoid using it for non-emergency reasons.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two drivers arrive at an open intersection at the same time, who goes first?
options: a:The driver on the left has the right-of-way.,b:The driver on the right has the right-of-way.,c:Either driver may proceed without yielding.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection the driver on the right has the right-of-way. Proceed only after they have safely passed.

question: If a driver is aggressive behind you, what is the best action?
options: a:Stare at the driver as he or she passes you.,b:Try to get out of the aggressive driver’s way.,c:Speed up as he or she is passing you.
note: Move out of the aggressive driver's path, avoid confrontation, and allow them to pass safely.

question: Under what circumstances may you drive around lowered gates at a railroad crossing?
options: a:When the lights stop flashing.,b:Under no circumstances.,c:When the train has passed and gates lift.
note: You must not go around lowered gates; they indicate an approaching train and trying to bypass them is illegal and dangerous.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a solid yellow arrow signal mean for turning drivers?
options: a:It means drivers may turn in the indicated direction without restriction.,b:It has the same meaning as a circular yellow traffic light—prepare to stop.,c:It is never used as a traffic signal.
note: A solid yellow arrow warns that the protected turning period is ending and you should prepare to stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it legal to cross a double solid yellow centerline to pass?
options: a:Yes.,b:No.,c:If there is no oncoming traffic.
note: You may not cross double solid yellow lines to pass; you can only cross to enter/exit driveways or turn off the roadway.

question: When you see a railroad crossing warning sign, what must you be prepared to do?
options: a:Be prepared to stop if a train is nearby.,b:Speed across the crossing before the train arrives.,c:Look for a way around lowered gates.
note: Railroad crossing warning signs mean you should slow, look, and be ready to stop if a train is approaching; never go around lowered gates.

question: What is a likely consequence of a second DWI conviction within five years in Missouri?
options: a:Lose your license for only 90 days.,b:Be restricted to driving on residential roads.,c:Be required to install an Ignition Interlock Device (IID) before reinstatement.
note: A second DWI within five years can mean a one-year suspension, heavy fines, possible jail time, and a required IID installation before license reinstatement.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, how should you steer?
options: a:Turn the steering wheel in the direction you want the vehicle to go.,b:Turn the steering wheel in the opposite direction of the skid.,c:Keep the front wheels straight.
note: When skidding, steer into the direction you want the car to travel and make adjustments as it straightens.

question: After purchasing a vehicle, within what time must you apply for the title?
options: a:Within 30 days.,b:Within six months.,c:Within one week.
note: You must apply for a vehicle title within 30 days of purchase; otherwise a penalty fee may apply.

question: Which recommendation would generally not improve nighttime driving safety?
options: a:Keep your windshield clean.,b:Be aware tinted windows reduce visibility in the dark.,c:Drive with your interior dome light on to read maps.
note: Keeping windows clean and limiting tint that reduces night visibility help safety; using interior lights while driving can impair visibility.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where should your vehicle be positioned when making a right turn?
options: a:Near the center of the street.,b:Close to the left side of the street.,c:As close to the right side of the road as possible.
note: When preparing to make a right turn, move as far right as possible without leaving the roadway or making unsafe maneuvers.

question: In traffic, what is the safest way to drive relative to the flow of traffic?
options: a:Drive faster than the flow of traffic.,b:Fluctuate your speed to keep alert.,c:Drive with the flow of traffic within posted limits.
note: Driving consistently with the flow of traffic (and within speed limits) reduces conflict and crash risk.

question: After a minor collision that leaves your vehicle blocking traffic, what should you do if possible?
options: a:Not move your vehicle under any circumstances.,b:Wait until the police arrive before moving your vehicle.,c:Move your vehicle off the traveled portion of the roadway.
note: If possible after a minor crash, move your vehicle out of traffic lanes to a safe location and identify yourself to others involved.

question: What lane entitlement do motorcycles have?
options: a:They are limited to the bicycle lane.,b:They are entitled to the same full lane width as other vehicles.,c:They get half the lane width.
note: Motorcycles are entitled to the full width of a lane just like any other vehicle.

question: What is the safest way to handle a driver tailgating you?
options: a:Gradually slow down or change lanes to encourage them to pass.,b:Slam on your brakes to signal them to back off.,c:Speed up to increase the gap ahead of you.
note: If someone follows too closely, ease off the gas and let them pass or change lanes when safe; avoid braking abruptly or escalating speed.

question: Which of these is a common cause of distracted driving?
options: a:Eating, drinking, or smoking.,b:Changing a radio station or CD.,c:Talking or texting on a cell phone.
note: Any activity that diverts your attention from driving—especially texting or phone use—creates dangerous distraction.

question: On which traffic signal do you have the right-of-way to turn left?
options: a:A solid green light,b:A flashing yellow light,c:A green arrow pointing left
note: A steady green arrow pointing left gives you the right-of-way to turn left while oncoming traffic is stopped by a red light.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a green turn arrow changes to a steady green light, what must you do before turning?
options: a:Yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians before turning.,b:You can no longer turn and must go straight.,c:You keep the right-of-way to turn without yielding.
note: When a green arrow becomes a solid green, you may still turn in that direction but must first yield to pedestrians and oncoming traffic.

question: At a light rail intersection, what should you always do?
options: a:Obey all traffic signals and look both ways before crossing tracks.,b:Drive around lowered crossing gates.,c:Assume trains will yield to cars.
note: Do not drive around lowered gates. Always obey signals, look both ways before crossing tracks, and share the road safely with trains, pedestrians, and bicyclists.

question: How can you reduce your chance of hydroplaning on wet roads?
options: a:Drive through shallow water quickly.,b:Drive more quickly.,c:Reduce your speed.
note: Hydroplaning is caused by excessive speed on wet surfaces; slow down to reduce the risk.

question: What is the fee for an instruction permit in Missouri?
note: An instruction permit in Missouri currently costs $3.50; it allows a learner to practice driving with a licensed supervising adult.

question: Which of the following is not an effect of alcohol on driving?
options: a:Your reflexes and reaction time slow down.,b:Your judgment of speed and distance is distorted.,c:You are less alert.
note: Alcohol impairs judgment, slows reaction times, and reduces alertness; all listed effects occur after drinking.

question: How can you help avoid rear-end collisions?
options: a:Avoid sudden stops and allow your vehicle to slow before applying brakes.,b:Ignore mirrors and focus on the vehicle ahead.,c:Brake sharply without warning to alert those behind you.
note: Avoid sudden stops by releasing the gas to let your vehicle slow and apply brakes smoothly, giving following drivers time to react.

question: Which actions improve safety when driving at night?
options: a:Increase following distance and ensure headlights are working.,b:Drive only if you are tired.,c:Use high beams at all times.
note: Night driving reduces visibility; increase following distance, avoid driving when fatigued, and make sure headlights and taillights are functioning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another vehicle on a two-lane road, when should you return to the driving lane?
options: a:Return to the driving lane when there is enough room between you and the vehicle you passed.,b:Return to the right side of the roadway immediately.,c:Remain in the left lane if you intend to turn left.
note: Return to your lane only when you can see the passed vehicle entirely in your rearview mirror and there is enough space.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing for a left turn, what checks should you make?
options: a:Signal early, check mirrors and watch for oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.,b:Only check your rearview mirror.,c:Speed up and cut across traffic.
note: Signal three to five seconds in advance, check mirrors, and yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians before turning left.

question: Where should you maintain a space cushion around your vehicle?
options: a:Only in front of your vehicle.,b:On all sides of your vehicle.,c:Only behind your vehicle.
note: Keep a cushion of space on all sides—front, back, and both sides—to give yourself time to react to hazards.

question: If a bicyclist disobeys traffic laws, what can happen?
options: a:They can be ticketed like motor vehicle drivers.,b:They are always given only a warning.,c:They are exempt from traffic laws.
note: Bicyclists have the same rights and responsibilities as drivers and can be cited for violating traffic laws.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Passing another vehicle is prohibited in which situation?
options: a:On hills and curves.,b:Only when there are no lane markings.,c:Whenever the vehicle ahead is signaling a turn.,d:When the road is wet.
note: It is unlawful and unsafe to pass on hills, curves, at intersections, and at railroad crossings where visibility is limited.

question: If you are driving in the left lane and want to move into the right lane, you should:
options: a:Check your mirrors, signal, and look over your right shoulder before changing lanes.,b:Check your mirrors, signal, and look over your left shoulder.,c:Check your mirrors only and then change lanes.,d:Signal and change lanes without looking.
note: When changing lanes, check mirrors, signal in advance, and glance into the blind spot in the direction you plan to move.

question: At a stop sign, which sequence of observations is recommended before proceeding?
options: a:Look right first, then left, then right again.,b:Check your rearview mirror first, then go.,c:Move as soon as the vehicle ahead moves.
note: When stopped, look right first because vehicles from the right are closer; then look left and right again before proceeding.

question: What does SATOP stand for?
options: a:Salt And Tar On Pavement.,b:Substance Abuse Traffic Offender Program.,c:Steer At The Other Point.
note: SATOP stands for Substance Abuse Traffic Offender Program, which is required for those convicted of certain alcohol-related driving offenses.

question: What should you do to be ready for anything ahead on the road?
options: a:Drive with your left foot resting lightly on the brake pedal.,b:Stare straight ahead at all times.,c:Continuously scan the entire road and roadsides.
note: Scan well ahead and to the sides; identifying hazards early gives you the time to react safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When are you required to stop your vehicle?
options: a:At stop signs, red lights, or when ordered by a traffic officer.,b:Only when other vehicles are present.,c:Only at intersections with no visible cross traffic.
note: You must stop at stop signs, red signals, or any time a traffic officer instructs you to stop.

question: Pentagon-shaped traffic signs are used to indicate:
options: a:No passing zones.,b:School zones and school crossings.,c:Speed limits.,d:Railroad crossings.
note: Pentagonal signs indicate school zones or school crossings; be extra alert for children and pedestrians near schools.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you legally pass another vehicle on the right?
options: a:When the vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is an available passing lane.,b:If it requires driving off the paved surface.,c:On a narrow bridge.
note: You may pass on the right when the vehicle ahead is turning left and there is room in a lane to the right, or on multilane roads traveling the same direction—never off pavement.

question: When changing lanes, what is the correct procedure?
options: a:Signal, check mirrors, and glance over your shoulder to verify your blind spot is clear.,b:Rely solely on your mirrors.,c:Signal at least 500 feet in advance in residential areas.
note: Signal appropriately, check mirrors, and look over your shoulder to ensure the blind spot is clear before moving into another lane.

question: What is the most common color for warning signs?
options: a:Yellow,b:Red,c:Green
note: Warning signs are commonly diamond-shaped with a yellow background and black symbols or lettering to alert drivers to hazards.

question: What does a black symbol on a yellow diamond-shaped sign generally tell you?
options: a:Warning about conditions on or near the road.,b:Directions to cities and towns.,c:Traffic laws and regulations.
note: Yellow diamond-shaped warning signs indicate conditions or hazards ahead that drivers should be aware of.

question: If your vehicle has ABS and you begin to lose traction, what should you do with the brake pedal?
options: a:Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.,b:Pump the brakes rapidly.,c:Release the brake pedal and coast.
note: With ABS, press and hold the brake pedal firmly; ABS will automatically pump the brakes to help maintain steering control.

question: What do downward-pointing triangular traffic signs usually indicate?
options: a:A school zone.,b:Yield to other traffic.,c:A construction area.
note: A downward-pointing triangle is used for yield signs: slow down and give the right-of-way when required.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are stopped in a line at a stop sign and there is no cross traffic after the vehicles ahead have gone through, what must you do?
options: a:You may proceed without stopping again.,b:You must stop again at the stop sign or stop line before going.,c:You may slowly roll past the stop sign.
note: You must always come to a complete stop at a stop sign and yield to traffic before proceeding.

question: When there is an oncoming car to your left and a bicyclist on your right, what should you do?
options: a:Pass the bicyclist immediately and squeeze by the car.,b:Let the oncoming car pass first, then pass the bicyclist so you handle only one hazard at a time.,c:Split the difference and squeeze between both.
note: Avoid trying to deal with two hazards at once: let the oncoming car pass, then pass the bicyclist safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a freeway, what is the best approach?
options: a:Use the ramp to accelerate to freeway speed and blend into traffic.,b:Proceed slowly and wait for a large gap.,c:Turn on hazard lights while merging.
note: Accelerate on the on-ramp to match freeway speeds and merge smoothly with the flow of traffic; yield to vehicles already on the freeway.

question: If involved in an accident, which actions should a driver take?
options: a:Stop their vehicle at or near the scene.,b:Not stand or walk in traffic lanes.,c:Turn off the ignition(s) of wrecked vehicles.,d:All of the above
note: After a crash stop at or near the scene, move vehicles out of traffic if possible, do not stand in lanes, and turn off ignitions of wrecked vehicles; call for help if needed.

question: Does the type of alcoholic beverage (beer, wine, liquor) change how it affects your reflexes and judgment?
options: a:No — impairment depends on the amount of alcohol in the bloodstream, not the beverage type.,b:Beer impairs you less than wine.,c:Hard ciders and mixed drinks impair you most.
note: All alcoholic beverages impair judgment and reflexes; the effect depends on the quantity of alcohol consumed, not the type of drink.

question: How should you respond to an approaching emergency vehicle using lights and siren?
options: a:Pull over to the side of the road and stop until it has passed.,b:Continue driving but attempt to remain out of its path.,c:Try to reach your destination before it gets to you.
note: Yield the right-of-way to emergency vehicles by pulling to the right edge of the road and stopping if possible; if in an intersection, drive through then pull over.

question: Approaching a railroad crossing with no flashing lights or gates, how should you proceed?
options: a:Always stop before crossing.,b:Cross quickly without looking.,c:Be prepared to yield to any approaching train and make sure you have room to clear the tracks.
note: If there are no gates or lights, be prepared to yield to trains and never start across the tracks unless there is room for your entire vehicle on the far side.

question: If you hit an unattended parked vehicle and cannot locate the owner, what must you do?
options: a:Have done as much as you can.,b:Leave a written notice with your name, address, and circumstances of the accident.,c:Must stay until the police arrive.
note: If you strike an unattended vehicle and cannot find the owner, leave a written notice with your contact information and details of the incident.

question: What do orange-colored signs generally indicate?
options: a:Construction, maintenance, or emergency operations ahead.,b:A school zone is ahead.,c:A railroad crossing is ahead.
note: Orange warning signs indicate construction, maintenance, or emergency operations and warn drivers to be prepared for changed traffic patterns.

question: What does a single dashed white line between lanes indicate?
options: a:Drivers may pass or change lanes if it is safe.,b:Drivers may not pass.,c:Lanes move in opposite directions.
note: Dashed white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and may be crossed to pass or change lanes when safe.

question: What must you do when an emergency vehicle is using sirens and flashing lights?
options: a:Have the right-of-way when using sirens, horns, and/or flashing lights.,b:May follow each other closely.,c:Ignore it if you are in the lane.
note: Yield the right-of-way to emergency vehicles using sirens or flashing lights. Follow any loudspeaker instructions and be aware emergency vehicles may travel together.

question: If another driver cuts you off in traffic, how should you respond?
options: a:Pull next to the driver and yell at them.,b:Let it go and continue driving safely.,c:Flash your high beams at them to show your displeasure.
note: To avoid road rage, accept minor traffic conflicts and continue driving safely rather than retaliating.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When two vehicles enter an intersection from different highways at the same time, which vehicle must yield?
options: a:Either one,b:The vehicle on the left,c:The vehicle on the right
note: When two vehicles enter at the same time, the driver on the left must yield the right-of-way to the driver on the right.

question: What is the effect of combining drugs with alcohol on crash risk?
options: a:It decreases the risk of causing a crash.,b:It increases the risk of causing a crash.,c:It has no effect on your ability to drive.
note: Combining drugs (prescription, over-the-counter, or illegal) with alcohol increases impairment and crash risk.

question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?
options: a:It is against the law to go around lowered gates at a crossing.,b:All railroad crossings are equipped with flashing red signals and gates.,c:You never have to stop when directed by a flagger.
note: You must obey warning devices and never go around lowered gates; not all crossings have gates or lights, and you must stop when directed by signs, lights, or a flagger.

question: When you hear or see an emergency vehicle approaching, what is the proper response?
options: a:Stop immediately and let the vehicle pass anywhere.,b:Drive as far toward the right side of the road as is safe and stop.,c:Proceed slowly and permit the vehicle to pass without pulling over.
note: On a two-lane or undivided highway, move as far to the right as possible and stop to allow emergency vehicles to pass; do not stop in an intersection.

question: What is the minimum age to obtain a motorcycle instruction permit in Missouri?
options: a:15 and one-half years old.,b:14 years old.,c:15 years old.
note: You must be at least 15½ years old to apply for a Missouri motorcycle instruction permit to learn to operate a motorcycle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must a driver do when approaching a steady red traffic light?
