options: a:Come to a complete stop; you may turn right on red unless a sign prohibits it.,b:Continue through if no other vehicles are present.,c:Stop only if a police officer is nearby.,d:Slow down and proceed with caution.
note: A steady red light requires a complete stop. After stopping, you may turn right on red unless a sign forbids it; running red lights is illegal and dangerous.

question: Where will the Driver License Bureau mail your renewal reminder postcard shortly before expiry?
options: a:To the mailing address on your driver record.,b:To the address on your last application.,c:To the address listed in the phone book.
note: Renewal reminders are mailed to the mailing address on your driver record; temporary instruction permits or commercial learner’s permits may not receive a mailed notice.

question: What should you adjust first when you get into a vehicle?
options: a:Your seat position.,b:Your mirrors only.,c:Your safety belt only.
note: Begin by adjusting your seat so you can see and reach controls comfortably; then adjust mirrors and steering wheel and buckle up.

question: When the center of the road has a solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line and the broken line is on your side, when may you pass?
options: a:Only in an emergency.,b:Only if you are on an expressway.,c:You may pass if traffic is clear and it is safe to do so.
note: When the broken line is adjacent to your lane you may cross it to pass, provided there is no oncoming traffic and it is safe.

question: If you fail the driving test three times, what will the examiner do?
options: a:The Department will require additional behind-the-wheel training before retesting.,b:The examiner will give you a Driving Skills Examination Report to send to the Department of Revenue.,c:You may retake the test the next day without restriction.,d:You must reapply for a learner's permit.
note: After three failures the examiner issues a Driving Skills Examination Report which you must send to the Department of Revenue; the department will then notify you if additional training is required.

question: Why must drivers be especially alert for motorcycles?
options: a:Motorcycles are smaller and harder to see and may be hidden in blind spots.,b:Motorcyclists rarely follow traffic laws.,c:Motorcyclists always travel at high speeds.
note: Motorcycles are smaller and more easily hidden in blind spots; their speed and distance can be harder to judge, so remain alert and allow extra space.

question: How does increasing your vehicle’s speed affect your field of vision?
options: a:It increases your field of vision.,b:It decreases your field of vision.,c:It makes it easier to see cross traffic.
note: As speed increases your peripheral vision narrows, so you must be extra alert to hazards and reduce speed as needed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do before changing lanes or passing on an interstate?
options: a:Stop on the shoulder if you are tired.,b:Always use cruise control.,c:Signal, check mirrors, and check your blind spots.
note: Signal, check mirrors, and glance into your blind spot before changing lanes. Only stop on the shoulder in an emergency and avoid cruise control in unsafe conditions.

question: What must you do when a flagger is controlling traffic in a construction zone?
options: a:Follow the flagger's directions.,b:Ignore the flagger and follow surrounding traffic.,c:Assume the flagger's directions are optional.
note: Obey flaggers and posted signs in construction zones; failure to do so is illegal and dangerous to workers and motorists.

question: If you are at fault in a crash and fail to pay for damages, what can happen to your driving privileges?
options: a:Your driver license and/or plates will be suspended for one year.,b:You will save money.,c:Your car will be repossessed automatically.
note: If you are at fault in an accident and don't pay damages, your license and/or plates may be suspended for one year unless you pay fees and show proof of settlement.

question: When stopped on an uphill slope, when should you allow a larger space cushion in front of your vehicle?
options: a:When stopped at a stop sign.,b:Whenever you are stopped on an incline.,c:When stopped at an intersection.
note: Allow extra space when stopped on an uphill slope so if the vehicle ahead rolls back, a collision is less likely.

question: What important attribute do large trucks have that car drivers should remember?
options: a:They have large blind spots.,b:They can stop more quickly than cars.,c:They do not need extra maneuvering room.
note: Large trucks have large blind spots around the front, sides, and rear. Avoid lingering in these areas and give trucks extra room to stop and turn.

question: What does a green traffic arrow mean for the lane it controls?
options: a:Traffic in that lane must turn in the direction of the arrow; its meaning is similar to a circular green.,b:It is used only on one-way streets.,c:You may proceed only if a circular green is also lit.
note: A green arrow has the same basic meaning as a green light but requires traffic in the indicated lane to turn in the arrow’s direction.

question: Regarding pedestrians, what responsibility does a driver have?
options: a:Make sure the pedestrian is always aware of their vehicle.,b:Always yield the right-of-way to pedestrians, even if they are wrong.,c:Yield only when the pedestrian is legally entitled to it.
note: Drivers must do everything reasonable to avoid striking pedestrians and must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in crosswalks or intersections.

question: When passing a large vehicle, what should a driver of a small vehicle be prepared for?
options: a:Loud noises.,b:Excess air pollution.,c:Wind gusts caused by the large vehicle.
note: Large vehicles can create strong air gusts that push smaller vehicles. Be ready to correct steering when approaching or passing large trucks.

question: How does smoking or preparing to smoke while driving affect your driving?
options: a:It does not affect driving abilities.,b:It helps maintain alertness.,c:It is a distracting activity.
note: Smoking while driving can distract you by requiring your hands or eyes off the road, increasing crash risk.

question: What effect does alcohol have on reflexes and reaction time?
options: a:It speeds them up.,b:It slows them down.,c:It has no effect.
note: Alcohol is a depressant that slows brain activity, including reflexes and reaction time important for driving.

question: If you are being tailgated, what is the safest action?
options: a:Brake abruptly to warn the tailgater.,b:Move to the right if an open lane exists; if not, slow gradually to encourage them to pass.,c:Increase your speed so the tailgater must back off.
note: If tailgated and a right lane is open, move over. If you cannot, wait until it's safe and then reduce speed gradually to encourage the tailgater to pass—never brake abruptly.

question: Regulatory signs are intended to:
options: a:Tell drivers what actions are required or prohibited.,b:Warn about upcoming hazards only.,c:Provide mileage information.
note: Regulatory signs communicate rules of the road—what drivers must or must not do—and must be obeyed.

question: What is the correct initial positioning when preparing to parallel park between two vehicles?
options: a:Stop even with the car in front of the space.,b:Turn wheels immediately to the left.,c:Back up directly into the space without aligning.
note: After checking traffic and signaling, stop parallel to the vehicle ahead of the intended parking space before turning to back into the spot.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a steady red traffic signal require you to do?
options: a:Stop before entering the intersection, stop line, or crosswalk.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:Yield only to pedestrians.
note: A red signal means stop; stop before the stop line, crosswalk, or intersection and remain stopped until the light changes unless turning where permitted.

question: If your vehicle’s right wheels leave the pavement, what is the correct way to return to the road?
options: a:Stop quickly and then turn sharply onto the pavement.,b:Take your foot off the accelerator, steer parallel to the road, slow, and ease back onto the pavement.,c:Accelerate and steer back on the road quickly.
note: Do not panic. Ease off the accelerator, keep the wheel straight, slow gradually, then steer gently back onto the roadway when safe.

question: What is the safest practice before backing a vehicle?
options: a:Walk to the rear of the vehicle to check for children or objects.,b:Honk the horn before shifting into reverse.,c:Rely solely on rearview mirrors.
note: Before you get in to back up, walk behind the vehicle to check for children and obstacles; backing is limited by reduced visibility.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a driver's left arm and hand are extended upward, what is that hand signal indicating?
options: a:Come to a stop.,b:Turn left.,c:Turn right.
note: A left arm extended upward signals an intended right turn.

question: What does a double solid yellow centerline mean?
options: a:Passing is not permitted from either direction.,b:Pedestrian crossing ahead.,c:Railroad crossing ahead.
note: Double solid yellow lines indicate no passing from either direction; you may cross only to turn left or enter/leave the roadway.

question: What can happen when alcohol is combined with another drug?
options: a:The effects of both the alcohol and the drug may be increased.,b:Nothing will happen.,c:The effects of both will always be reduced.,d:Only alcohol effects increase.
note: Combining alcohol with other drugs can amplify impairment; even small amounts may have large effects when mixed with medications.

question: What color lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction?
options: a:White.,b:Yellow.,c:Red.
note: White lines separate lanes moving in the same direction; broken white lines may be crossed for lane changes.

question: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an approaching emergency vehicle, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down until it passes.,b:Pull to the right side of the road and stop.,c:Motion for the emergency vehicle to pass ahead of you.
note: Yield the right-of-way to emergency vehicles using lights or sirens. Immediately move to the right and stop until they have passed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking downhill on a two-way street, how should you turn your wheels?
options: a:Turn your wheels to the right.,b:Turn your wheels to the left.,c:Keep your wheels pointed straight ahead.
note: On a downhill slope, turn the front wheels toward the curb so a roll will bring the vehicle to a stop at the curb.

question: What do functioning brake lights communicate to drivers behind you?
options: a:That you are slowing down or stopping.,b:That you are changing lanes.,c:That your emergency brake is engaged.
note: Brake lights signal to following drivers that you are slowing or stopping; ensure they are always working properly.

question: What defines a driver's blind spot?
options: a:An area you cannot see without moving your head.,b:The area directly behind your vehicle.,c:The view you see in your rearview mirror.
note: Blind spots are areas the driver cannot see without physically moving their head and checking.

question: How do worn or bald tires affect vehicle performance?
options: a:They can increase your stopping distance.,b:They can make turning more difficult.,c:They are likely to hydroplane.
note: Tires with insufficient tread can increase stopping distance, reduce cornering ability, and raise hydroplaning risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, who yields?
options: a:The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.,b:The vehicle on the right must yield to the vehicle on the left.,c:Drivers must make hand motions to communicate with each other.
note: When two vehicles arrive at the same time, the vehicle on the left should yield to the vehicle on the right.

question: Is it legal to drink alcoholic beverages in a vehicle on a public highway?
options: a:No, it is illegal to consume or possess an open alcoholic beverage on a public road.,b:Yes, if you are a passenger in the back seat.,c:Yes, if you are not driving the vehicle.
note: Missouri law prohibits consuming or possessing an alcoholic beverage on public roads or sidewalks and prohibits open containers in areas normally occupied by the driver or passengers.

question: Where are you prohibited from parking?
options: a:In a parking lot.,b:On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.,c:On a hill.,d:Within 12 inches of the curb when on the street.
note: It is unlawful to park on a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane. When parking on the street, you must park within 12 inches of the curb.

question: How should you check blind spots when changing lanes?
options: a:Turn your head to look over your shoulder into the blind spot.,b:Rely only on your inside rearview mirror.,c:Use only the outside mirror.
note: Turn your head to check blind spots before every lane change; mirrors alone may not reveal vehicles in the blind spot.

question: Why should drivers be extra alert for motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians?
options: a:They always have the right-of-way.,b:They obey different traffic laws than larger motor vehicles.,c:They are often harder to see in traffic.
note: Smaller road users can be difficult to spot and may have less-visible lighting; be especially vigilant around them.

question: How should you check your blind spot before changing lanes to the left?
options: a:Glance over your left shoulder.,b:Check your right-side mirror.,c:Use only the inside rearview mirror.
note: To verify the lane is clear, quickly glance over the shoulder in the direction you plan to move to reveal vehicles hidden from mirrors.

question: What must you do if a bus is signaling to re-enter traffic after stopping to load or unload?
options: a:Yield and allow the bus to re-enter safely.,b:Honk to alert the bus driver.,c:Maintain speed and position.
note: Yield to transit vehicles signaling to re-enter traffic after passenger loading or unloading; change lanes or slow to provide a safe gap.

question: Where must you keep proof of liability insurance while operating a vehicle?
options: a:In a safety deposit box at the bank.,b:In your vehicle whenever it is being operated.,c:At your place of employment.
note: Missouri law requires drivers to carry proof of liability insurance in the vehicle while operating it.

question: What should you adjust first when preparing to drive a vehicle?
options: a:Your seat position so you can see and reach controls.,b:Your rearview mirror only.,c:The steering wheel only.
note: Set your seat first so you can see the road and reach the pedals and controls comfortably, then adjust mirrors and the steering wheel as needed.

question: When a stopped school bus extends its stop arm and displays stop signals, drivers should:
options: a:Continue driving when they think most kids are done exiting.,b:Come to a complete stop and wait to proceed.,c:Honk their horn before passing the bus on its left.
note: When a school bus is stopped with signals, you must stop and remain stopped until the bus resumes motion and the signals are withdrawn.

question: A leaking exhaust system can:
options: a:Cause excessive oil use.,b:Require your vehicle to need tune-ups sooner.,c:Make you drowsy or expose you to toxic fumes.,d:Improve fuel efficiency.
note: Exhaust leaks can allow toxic gases into the vehicle, causing drowsiness or even death; have leaks repaired immediately.

question: What is distracted driving characterized as?
options: a:Very uncommon.,b:Extremely risky behavior.,c:Nothing to be concerned about.
note: Distracted driving is extremely risky and significantly increases the chance of crashes.

question: Which of the following types of drugs can affect your driving ability?
options: a:Only illegal drugs,b:Only over-the-counter cold remedies,c:Prescription, over-the-counter, and illegal drugs can all impair driving.
note: Many drugs—illegal, prescription, and over-the-counter—can impair driving. Driving under the influence of any impairing drug may be a crime.

question: How can you avoid collisions with vehicles in your blind spots?
options: a:Turn your head and glance over your shoulder to confirm the blind spot is clear.,b:Adjust your rearview mirrors more frequently.,c:Honk before changing lanes.
note: Never rely only on mirrors; turn your head briefly to check the blind spot before changing lanes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A flashing red light is equivalent to which traffic control device?
options: a:A stop sign.,b:A yield sign.,c:A solid red light.
note: A flashing red traffic signal requires a full stop and yields the same action as a stop sign.

question: Which combination provides the most protection in a crash?
options: a:An airbag only.,b:A lap and shoulder belt only.,c:A lap/shoulder belt used with an airbag.
note: Seat belts significantly increase survival chances; airbags provide additional protection when used with lap/shoulder belts.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a traffic light turns from green to yellow as you approach, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to make the intersection.,b:Prepare to stop if it is safe to do so.,c:Stop abruptly in the center of the intersection.
note: A steady yellow means the light will turn red soon; be prepared to stop if you can do so safely.

question: To reduce fatigue on a long trip, what is recommended?
options: a:Keep driving but do arm exercises every hour.,b:Stop and rest about every two hours.,c:Drive with one eye closed to stay alert.
note: To avoid fatigue, stop every two hours for a short break; if drowsy, pull off the road and rest.

question: When crossing railroad tracks, what should you do to be safe?
options: a:Cross quickly when a train is approaching.,b:Look and listen both ways and only proceed when it is safe.,c:Only look both ways when the red light is flashing.,d:Turn on your headlights before crossing.
note: Always look and listen for trains from both directions, watch for warning signals, and never cross until you are certain it is safe.

question: How is drinking and driving best described?
options: a:A serious traffic safety problem.,b:A minor traffic safety problem.,c:Safe if you have only had a few drinks.
note: Driving after drinking or taking impairing drugs is a serious safety hazard and significantly increases crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must not drive faster than:
options: a:A speed that is reasonable and prudent for existing conditions.,b:The posted maximum speed only.,c:A speed that is slower than surrounding traffic regardless of conditions.
note: Drivers must choose a speed that is safe for current conditions (weather, traffic, road surface), not just the posted limit.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you need to make a turn but you are not in the proper lane, what should you do?
options: a:Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.,b:Turn on your blinker and make the turn from your current lane.,c:Drive to the next intersection and then make the turn from the proper lane.
note: Do not make last-minute turns or sudden lane changes. Proceed to the next intersection and make the turn from the correct lane.

question: When sharing the road with large trucks, remember that trucks generally:
options: a:Require less time to pass on a downgrade.,b:Require a smaller turning radius than smaller vehicles.,c:Require longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles do.
note: Due to their mass, trucks need more distance to slow or stop than passenger vehicles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, where should your vehicle end up?
options: a:In the right lane of the one-way street.,b:In the center of the street.,c:In the left lane of the one-way street.,d:In any lane available.
note: Complete the turn into the lane closest to the lane you came from—when turning left onto a one-way street, end up in the left lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where should you begin slowing down when exiting a highway?
options: a:On the main road, just before the exit lane.,b:Once you have moved into the exit lane.,c:Once you see a toll booth.
note: Enter the exit lane in advance and begin reducing speed after you are already in the exit lane.

question: Which of the following is true regarding sudden weather changes?
options: a:A sudden change in weather calls for a change in your driving.,b:You should not adjust your speed when it rains.,c:Be less aware of vehicles behind you in bad weather.,d:Weather does not affect stopping distance.
note: If weather changes suddenly, adjust your driving—slow down in rain or fog and be aware of vehicles behind you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must drivers yield to pedestrians?
options: a:Only when the pedestrian is in a marked crosswalk.,b:Only if the pedestrian is on the same side of the road as the driver.,c:Drivers must yield to pedestrians in the street even if they cross carelessly.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in the roadway; exercise caution even when pedestrians are not strictly following rules.

question: If you are on a one-way street and an emergency vehicle using flashing lights approaches, what must you do?
options: a:Drive with your flashers turned on.,b:Drive toward the nearest roadside and stop.,c:Speed up and take the nearest exit.
note: On a one-way street you must drive toward the nearest roadside and stop to allow the emergency vehicle to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which is a good general rule regarding passing other vehicles?
options: a:Drive with the flow of traffic and pass only when necessary and safe.,b:Always pass on the right when possible.,c:Try to get to the front of slow-moving traffic quickly.
note: Passing increases collision risk; travel with the flow of traffic within legal limits and pass only when safe and necessary.

question: What type of signs require drivers to obey the indicated instruction?
options: a:Regulatory signs.,b:Warning signs.,c:Information signs.,d:Guide signs.
note: Regulatory signs tell drivers what they must or must not do; failing to obey them can result in penalties.

question: If you discover a vehicle defect that could affect safe operation, what should you do?
options: a:Have the defect corrected as soon as possible.,b:Drive slower and defer repair.,c:Correct it only when you can afford it.
note: Any defect affecting safety should be corrected promptly before driving to ensure safe vehicle operation.

question: Which factors affect braking distance?
options: a:The speed your vehicle is traveling.,b:The condition of your brakes and tires.,c:The condition of the pavement.
note: Braking distance depends on speed, vehicle braking/tire condition, and roadway surface condition; all are important.

question: A “No stopping” sign means you may stop only under what circumstance?
options: a:Only to unload packages.,b:To avoid conflict with other traffic or to obey traffic control.,c:To discharge passengers whenever you wish.
note: A 'No stopping' sign means you may only stop to obey a traffic signal or officer or to avoid conflict with other traffic—not for loading or convenience.

question: If your wheels slip off the paved road onto the shoulder, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down gradually, then steer back onto the pavement when safe.,b:Jerk the steering wheel to force the vehicle back onto the pavement.,c:Slam on the brakes immediately.
note: Keep control: reduce speed gently, then when safe, steer back onto the road—do not make sudden steering or braking maneuvers.

question: When passing a stopped emergency vehicle with lights flashing on the roadway shoulder, what must you do?
options: a:Stay in your lane and continue at the same speed.,b:Slow down and, if possible, change lanes away from the stopped emergency vehicle.,c:Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
note: Move over a lane if it is safe; otherwise, slow to a safe speed below the limit and give the stopped vehicle as much space as possible.

question: What does a solid white center line on a multi-lane roadway usually mean?
options: a:It separates lanes moving in the same direction and indicates passing is not permitted.,b:It separates traffic moving in opposite directions.,c:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers may pass freely.
note: White lines separate lanes moving in the same direction; a solid line indicates lane changes or passing are discouraged or prohibited.

question: A single broken white line down the center of a roadway indicates:
options: a:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers may pass when it is safe.,b:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and passing is prohibited.,c:Lanes move in opposite directions and passing is allowed.,d:The line marks the edge of the roadway.
note: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A broken (dashed) line permits lane changes and passing when safe.

question: What is the best way to reduce the chance of hydroplaning on wet roads?
options: a:Slow down and maintain tires in good condition while watching for standing water.,b:Use cruise control to maintain steady speed.,c:Drive faster to get across puddles quickly.
note: Reduce speed, ensure tires are properly inflated and treaded, and avoid standing water to lower hydroplaning risk.

question: When must you pull over and allow an emergency vehicle to pass?
options: a:Only if it is following you.,b:Only if it is approaching from the opposite direction.,c:Regardless of its direction, pull to the right edge and stop.
note: You must pull to the right and stop for an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, no matter its direction of approach.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a \No standing\" sign allow you to do at that location?"
options: a:You may never stop your vehicle there.,b:You may stop temporarily only to pick up or discharge passengers.,c:You may park there if the driver remains in the vehicle.
note: A \No standing\" sign allows temporary stopping only to pick up or drop off passengers; parking is not allowed."

question: Which pavement marking or lane control device directs drivers into proper turn lanes?
options: a:Arrow pavement markings and lane arrows.,b:Flashing red lights.,c:White lines on the side of the road.
note: Arrows on the pavement and lane markings direct drivers into the correct lanes for turning or going straight.

question: Lack of sleep affects driving ability similarly to which of the following?
options: a:The effect that alcohol has.,b:The effect that amphetamines have.,c:The effect that anger has.
note: Fatigue impairs driving similar to alcohol. For example, 18 hours awake can impair driving about the same as a 0.05% BAC.

question: What is the key principle of speed management for curves?
options: a:Slow down before entering the curve.,b:Maintain the posted speed through the curve then brake at the end.,c:Accelerate upon entering the curve.
note: Reduce your speed before entering a curve to compensate for inertia and maintain control while turning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you see a Merging traffic sign on a freeway, what should you do?
options: a:Always remain at your present speed.,b:Make room for entering vehicles—move over a lane if safe.,c:Honk at incoming traffic.
note: On multi-lane roadways, allow merging traffic room by changing lanes if it is safe to do so.

question: Which type of sign warns drivers about potentially hazardous conditions ahead?
options: a:Information signs.,b:Warning signs.,c:Regulatory signs.
note: Warning signs alert drivers to hazardous or unusual road conditions; obey them to reduce accident risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What determines the space you need to cross traffic safely?
options: a:Road and weather conditions, and oncoming traffic.,b:Presence of a stop sign only.,c:Whether you used your turn signal.
note: The gap needed to cross traffic depends on road surface, weather, and the speed and distance of oncoming vehicles.

question: On a two-lane highway, when must you stop for a school bus displaying flashing red lights?
options: a:If you are both driving on a two-lane highway and its red lights are flashing.,b:When it approaches you, even if its lights are not flashing.,c:When it is parked on the shoulder with no one in it.
note: On two-lane roads, traffic in both directions must stop when a school bus displays flashing red lights and the stop arm is extended.

question: What color are guide (destination) signs?
options: a:Green,b:Red,c:Yellow
note: Guide signs that give directional and mileage information to destinations have a green background with white letters and symbols.

question: What is the safest approach to driving on slick roads?
options: a:Accelerate quickly.,b:Change lanes quickly.,c:Take turns more slowly than usual.
note: On slick surfaces, reduce speed and take turns more slowly than under normal conditions to maintain control.

question: What should drivers do when driving in bad weather regarding following distance?
options: a:Increase their speed to arrive sooner.,b:Decrease their following distance.,c:Increase their following distance.
note: In bad weather increase following distance to allow more time and space to stop safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it permissible to pass another vehicle using the road shoulder?
options: a:Under no circumstances.,b:When the vehicle ahead is making a left turn.,c:To go around a slow-moving vehicle.
note: Never pass another vehicle by driving on the shoulder; other drivers will not expect you there and it is unsafe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A flashing red traffic signal at an intersection has the same requirement as which sign?
options: a:A stop sign.,b:A slow sign.,c:A yield sign.
note: A flashing red signal requires the same action as a stop sign: come to a complete stop and yield as appropriate.

question: A driver’s license may be suspended if the driver does what regarding a chemical test?
options: a:Refuses to submit to a chemical test when requested.,b:Drives 10 mph over the speed limit.,c:Honks a horn in a residential area after midnight.
note: By driving in Missouri you consent to chemical testing when requested; refusal results in license suspension (usually one year).

question: At dusk or on overcast days, drivers should do which of the following?
options: a:Turn on headlights.,b:Use only parking lights.,c:Use four-way flashers.,d:Keep vehicle lights off.
note: Turn on your headlights; use low beams within 1,000 feet of oncoming vehicles and within 500 feet of vehicles you are following.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you use your turn signals?
options: a:Only when changing lanes.,b:Only when pulling into or out of a parking space.,c:Whenever you change direction—changing lanes, parking, or entering traffic.
note: Use turn signals for any lateral movement: changing lanes, pulling into/out of parking, or pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area.

question: Which is true about drowsy drivers?
options: a:Opening a window or turning up the radio will reliably keep them alert.,b:Drinking strong black coffee will always keep them safe to drive.,c:Drowsy drivers can operate so poorly that they may appear to be intoxicated.
note: Drowsiness can impair driving to the point of resembling intoxication; simple measures like windows or radio usually aren’t enough.

question: If a driver's left arm is extended downwards, what is that hand signal indicating?
options: a:Turning left.,b:Stopping or slowing.,c:Turning right.
note: A left arm extended down indicates the driver intends to stop or slow; adjust your driving if following that vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you yield to other drivers?
options: a:When entering a street from a garage, alley, or driveway.,b:Only when they are on a road to your left.,c:Only when you have a yield sign.
note: You must yield when entering a roadway from a garage, driveway, or alley and must also yield to pedestrians on an intersecting sidewalk.

question: If the driver ahead is distracted and driving with one hand while talking to a passenger, what is the safest response?
options: a:Give the vehicle extra space because their attention is reduced.,b:Follow exactly the same driving style.,c:Attempt to pass immediately.
note: Allow extra following distance around distracted drivers because they have reduced reaction capability, increasing crash risk.

question: Why is maintaining a space cushion around your vehicle important?
options: a:It prevents distractions from nearby vehicles.,b:It gives you time to react to unexpected situations.,c:It keeps traffic flowing faster.
note: A space cushion gives you time and room to react if other drivers make mistakes or hazards appear.

question: To lessen the effects of headlight glare at night, where should you direct your gaze?
options: a:Straight ahead.,b:At the center of the road.,c:Toward the right side of the road ahead.
note: If oncoming drivers do not dim their lights, look toward the right side of the road to avoid being blinded by glare.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When an officer is directing traffic at an intersection with working signals, you should:
options: a:Follow the directions given by the officer.,b:Obey the traffic lights instead of the officer.,c:Honk at the officer to get more information.,d:Wait for a written instruction.
note: An officer's directions take precedence over traffic signals; obey the officer to keep traffic moving safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What are points on your driving record?
options: a:They are beneficial when applying for driving jobs.,b:Points are added to your driving record after convictions and can lead to loss of driving privileges.,c:They are nothing to worry about.
note: Points are added after traffic convictions; accumulating too many can result in license suspension or revocation.

question: Why must you be more cautious when driving at night?
options: a:There is a larger volume of traffic at night.,b:Traffic moves faster at night.,c:Drivers cannot see as well in the dark.
note: Visibility is reduced at night. Use headlights from one half hour after sunset until one half hour before sunrise or whenever people or vehicles are not visible for 500 feet.

question: How do you officially indicate you want to be an organ donor on your license?
options: a:Have two witnesses sign the back of your license.,b:Complete the organ donor information on the back of your license when applying or renewing.,c:Discuss your decision with your next of kin only.
note: You can register as an organ donor by completing the donor section on your license or registering online and informing family of your decision.

question: When passing a bicyclist, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down and give the bicyclist as much space as possible.,b:Honk to alert the bicyclist that you are passing.,c:Drive in the bicycle lane until you can safely pass.
note: When passing a bicyclist, reduce speed and provide as much lateral space as practical; do not crowd or pass too quickly since bicycles are vulnerable to being pushed off course.

question: The act of turning your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes is:
options: a:Unnecessary.,b:A good driving habit.,c:A bad driving habit.,d:Required only when reversing.
note: Checking blind spots by glancing over your shoulder before lane changes is an important supplement to mirror checks.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering the street from a driveway, what must you do?
options: a:Stop before entering and proceed only when no pedestrians or vehicles are approaching.,b:Honk to alert approaching traffic.,c:Drive slowly and expect approaching vehicles to yield.
note: You must stop before entering the roadway from a driveway and yield to any approaching vehicles or pedestrians.

question: After a school bus unloads children and its stop arm is extended, what should you do?
options: a:Proceed once the bus driver waves.,b:Watch for children walking along the side of the road and proceed with caution.,c:Accelerate quickly to clear the area.
note: After a bus stops and unloads, watch carefully for children who may be walking along the roadway before proceeding.

question: For a driver age 21 or older, what blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is illegal to drive at or above in Missouri?
options: a:0.05 percent.,b:0.08 percent.,c:0.02 percent.
note: In Missouri it is illegal for drivers 21 or older to operate a vehicle with a BAC of 0.08% or higher.

question: How can you ensure your physical condition will not make your driving unsafe?
options: a:Keep physically fit and have regular physical examinations.,b:Know the effect of any medicine on your driving ability.,c:Drive within your physical limitations.
note: Stay aware of health, medication effects, and personal limits; seek medical advice and drive only when safe.

question: In which situations is it important to reduce speed?
options: a:On narrow or winding roads, intersections, railroad crossings, and when the road is wet or slippery.,b:Only when you see road signs advising you to slow down.,c:Only at night.
note: Reduce speed on narrow or winding roads, near intersections or railroad crossings, and when road conditions, weather, or visibility make driving hazardous.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are already inside an intersection and the signal turns yellow, what is the appropriate action?
options: a:Stop in the center of the intersection.,b:Continue carefully through the intersection.,c:Turn on hazard lights and back up.
note: If a steady yellow appears while you are already in the intersection, continue through carefully.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Approaching an uncontrolled intersection, you should:
options: a:Maintain your speed and proceed.,b:Slow down, check left-right-left, and yield to vehicles from the right as needed.,c:Always come to a full stop.,d:Only yield if another vehicle signals.
note: At intersections with no signs or signals, be prepared to yield to vehicles on your right; cover the brake and look both ways to avoid a crash.

question: When preparing to change lanes, what should you do?
options: a:Signal your intention, check blind spots, and ensure the lane is clear before moving.,b:Check your blind spot after beginning the lane change.,c:Signal only after you have moved into the lane.
note: Signal several seconds in advance, check mirrors and blind spots, then change lanes only when it is safe to do so.

question: If another car is about to hit you, what is the correct way to warn them?
options: a:Wave your arms.,b:Use your emergency lights.,c:Sound your horn.
note: Use your horn to warn others when you believe a collision is imminent and they may not see you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If your vehicle's turn signals stop working, how should you indicate turns?
options: a:Use your horn.,b:Turn on your headlights.,c:Use hand signals to show your turns.
note: If your turn signals fail, use the prescribed hand signals to indicate turns until signals are repaired.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you respond to a flashing red traffic light at an intersection?
options: a:Slow down but keep moving.,b:Come to a full stop and proceed when it is safe.,c:Continue without stopping.
note: A flashing red light has the same meaning as a stop sign: stop, yield the right-of-way, then go when safe.

question: If you begin to feel tired while driving, the best thing to do is to:
options: a:Get some coffee and keep driving.,b:Open your windows and continue.,c:Stop driving and rest.,d:Turn up the radio and stay alert.
note: Fatigue impairs driving similar to alcohol—pull over in a safe place and rest rather than trying to push on.

question: What should you do when you approach an accident scene?
options: a:Do not stop unless you are involved or emergency help has not yet arrived.,b:Pull over and watch the scene.,c:Stop and get out to see what happened.
note: Do not stop to gawk; only stop if you are involved or if emergency help has not yet arrived. Keep attention on driving and watch for people near the roadway.

question: If you experience a tire blowout while driving, what is the correct response?
options: a:Take your foot off the gas and keep steering straight.,b:Immediately apply the brakes hard.,c:Gradually slow down and pull off the road when safe.
note: If a tire blows out, ease off the gas, avoid heavy braking, gradually reduce speed, and pull off the roadway when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an intersection without a traffic signal, if a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing, who must yield?
options: a:Whoever started moving last.,b:The driver must yield to the pedestrian.,c:Whoever is slower.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing without a traffic signal; prioritize pedestrian safety.

question: What color are pavement markings that separate traffic moving in opposite directions?
options: a:Yellow,b:White,c:Both yellow and white
note: Yellow pavement markings are used to separate opposing directions of traffic.

question: Which of the following can help reduce road rage and aggressive driving?
options: a:Allowing extra travel time.,b:Obeying posted speed limits.,c:Using proper turn signals.,d:All of the above
note: Allow extra time, obey speed limits, and use signals—these measures help reduce stress and the likelihood of aggressive driving encounters.

question: On average, how many standard alcoholic drinks does the body process per hour?
options: a:Three drinks per hour.,b:One drink per hour.,c:Two drinks per hour.
note: The average person metabolizes roughly one standard drink per hour, though many factors affect impairment and BAC.

question: When parked facing uphill with a curb, how should you position your front wheels?
options: a:Turn the wheels sharply away from the curb.,b:Turn your wheels sharply toward the curb.,c:Keep the front wheels straight ahead.
note: Facing uphill with a curb, turn the front wheels away from the curb so the vehicle will roll into the curb if it moves.

question: In foggy conditions, which headlight setting should you use?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:Hazard lights.,c:High beam headlights.
note: Use low beam headlights in fog (or reduced visibility) because high beams reflect back and reduce visibility.

question: What does the term \No zone\" refer to?"
options: a:A roadway with stereo volume restrictions.,b:Blind spots around a truck or bus.,c:A special reduced-speed zone.
note: Trucks and buses have blind spots on the sides, front, and rear where other vehicles may be invisible—these are called \No zones.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is signaling before turning, changing lanes, or pulling from a curb required?
options: a:Only necessary if other traffic is present.,b:Required by law and a good habit.,c:Necessary only during the maneuver, not beforehand.
note: You must signal at least 100 feet before turning or moving laterally; signaling is both the law and good practice.

question: If you hear an emergency vehicle siren but cannot see it, what should you do?
options: a:Keep driving until you see the vehicle.,b:Pull to the curb and look to see if it is on your street.,c:Slow down and do not stop until you can locate it.
note: If you hear but cannot locate an emergency vehicle, safely pull to the right and stop to determine whether it is coming toward you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the correct way to enter a freeway from an entrance ramp?
options: a:Signal, yield to existing traffic, and enter at the same speed traffic is moving.,b:Signal and enter because freeway traffic must yield to you.,c:Stop at the end of the ramp to wait for a large gap.
note: When merging, signal, match the speed of highway traffic when safe, and yield to vehicles already on the freeway.

question: On a vertical traffic signal, what is the top-to-bottom order of lights?
options: a:Green, yellow, red.,b:Red, yellow, green.,c:Red, green, yellow.
note: A vertically arranged traffic light always has red on top, yellow in the middle, and green on the bottom.

question: If an approaching driver fails to dim their high beams, where should you look?
options: a:At the wheels of the approaching vehicle.,b:Toward the right side of the road.,c:Toward the left side of the road.
note: Glance toward the right edge of the roadway to avoid being blinded while still keeping enough sight of the road to stay on course.

question: If you leave your vehicle unattended, what must you do with the ignition?
options: a:Turn off the engine.,b:Lock the ignition and remove the key.,c:Set the parking brake.
note: When leaving a vehicle unattended you must stop the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you cross a solid yellow center line?
options: a:Only to make a turn.,b:At any time to pass slower traffic.,c:During daytime hours only.
note: Solid yellow lines generally prohibit passing; you may cross a solid yellow only to make a turn (such as into a driveway or side road).

question: If you are ordered to install an ignition interlock device (IID), who pays for installation and monthly inspections?
options: a:You must pay for installation and monthly maintenance costs.,b:The court pays for installation.,c:The arresting officer pays the fees.
note: If required to install an IID, the driver is responsible for all installation and monthly servicing costs as a condition of reinstatement.

question: What is a likely administrative consequence after a first-time DWI conviction?
options: a:Administrative license suspension for 90 days.,b:A $50 fine.,c:No penalty if it's your first offense.
note: A first-time DWI conviction leads to an administrative license suspension of 90 days; court penalties can be additional.

question: A flashing yellow arrow for left turns means:
options: a:You should merge into the lane in the arrow's direction.,b:You must come to a complete stop before turning.,c:You may turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
note: A flashing yellow arrow permits left turns after you yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians—do not assume you have a protected turn.

question: Which behavior describes an inattentive driver?
options: a:Staring at objects off the roadway or daydreaming while driving.,b:Maintaining eye contact during a conversation with a passenger.,c:Only watching the vehicle ahead.
note: Avoid distractions such as daydreaming, looking at passengers, reading, or sightseeing. Continually scan the road and mirrors to stay attentive.

question: Which statement best describes the slow-moving vehicle emblem?
options: a:A circular green sign.,b:A rectangular red sign.,c:A reflective orange triangle mounted on the vehicle.
note: Slow-moving vehicles display a reflective orange triangle to warn that they travel at 25 mph or less.

question: What do pennant-shaped traffic signs usually indicate?
options: a:School zones.,b:Speed limits.,c:No passing zones.
note: Pennant-shaped signs mounted on the left side of the roadway indicate no passing zones.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Advisory speed signs attached to curves indicate:
options: a:They may be ignored in rainy, snowy, or icy conditions.,b:Recommended speeds for safe travel in the curve under normal conditions.,c:They have a triangular shape.
note: Advisory speed plates recommend safe speeds for curves under normal conditions but you should slow further in poor weather.

question: If your vehicle does not have ABS and you need to stop quickly, what technique should you use?
options: a:Firmly pump the brakes to stop while retaining steering control.,b:Hold down the brake pedal so it locks up.,c:Tap the brakes lightly while steering.
note: For non-ABS vehicles, pumping the brakes (applying and releasing) helps avoid wheel lockup while allowing steering control during an emergency stop.

question: When stopped in a line of traffic at a railroad crossing with no signals or gates, what must you ensure?
options: a:You have the right-of-way and do not need to check for trains.,b:You may pass slower drivers while crossing the track.,c:There is enough space for your vehicle to completely clear the tracks without stopping.
note: Before entering tracks, make sure there is room on the far side so you won't be stuck on the rails; never pass at a crossing.

question: If you must reduce speed on a slippery road, what should you do first?
options: a:Apply the parking brake.,b:Firmly apply your brakes.,c:Take your foot off the gas pedal.
note: On slippery surfaces, first remove your foot from the accelerator; then brake gently if more slowing is required.

question: Where do you go to take the Missouri driver examination?
options: a:Any Missouri State Highway Patrol examination station.,b:Any Department of Transportation office.,c:Any Missouri contract office.
note: Driver examinations in Missouri are administered by the Missouri State Highway Patrol; contact the MSHP or Department of Revenue for locations.

question: Which action helps reduce the risk of hydroplaning?
options: a:Replace tires with bad tread.,b:Do not speed when roads are wet.,c:Ignore tire air pressure.
note: Reducing speed on wet roads lowers the risk of hydroplaning; good tread and proper tire pressure also help.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A steady yellow traffic light warns that which light will soon appear?
options: a:A flashing yellow light.,b:A steady red light.,c:A steady green light.
note: A steady yellow warns that the signal is about to turn red; prepare to stop if it is safe to do so.

question: When may you cross a dashed white line?
options: a:When it is safe to change lanes.,b:Only during daylight hours.,c:At any time regardless of conditions.
note: Broken white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and may be crossed when it is safe to change lanes.

question: When should you drive below the posted speed limit?
options: a:When anything makes driving conditions less than perfect.,b:Only when entering a highway.,c:Whenever you see a police car.,d:Never.
note: Reduce speed when visibility or road conditions are poor; you can be cited for driving too fast for conditions even if under the posted limit.

question: Before changing lanes on a highway, you should:
options: a:Signal, check rearview and side mirrors, and glance over your shoulder into the blind spot.,b:Signal and immediately change lanes if mirrors look clear.,c:Check only the rearview mirror and then change lanes.,d:Honk before changing lanes to warn others.
note: Signal well in advance, check mirrors, and check the blind spot by looking over your shoulder before changing lanes.

question: If another person is injured in an accident, how should you handle them?
options: a:Move them away from the scene immediately.,b:Do not move them unnecessarily; keep them warm and provide first aid if trained.,c:Always leave injured persons where they are and walk away.
note: Avoid moving injured people unless necessary; keep them warm and provide first aid (e.g., control severe bleeding) until help arrives.

question: When a transit bus is signaling to pull back into traffic after a stop, what must you do?
options: a:Yield to the bus so it can re-enter traffic.,b:Honking is required to alert the bus.,c:Remain in your lane and maintain speed.
note: Drivers must yield—change lanes, slow, or stop if necessary—to allow transit buses safely to re-enter the main roadway after loading or unloading passengers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you cross a single broken white or yellow line?
options: a:When doing so would interfere with traffic.,b:When turning left into a driveway.,c:When it is safe and does not interfere with traffic.
note: You may cross a single broken line to pass or change lanes provided it is safe and does not impede traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How far in advance should you signal before making a turn?
options: a:35 feet,b:50 feet,c:At least 100 feet before the turn.
note: Signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes or turning so other drivers can react to your intentions.

question: Which color line divides lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions?
options: a:Red.,b:White.,c:Yellow.
note: Yellow lines divide traffic moving in opposite directions; white lines divide lanes moving the same direction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a double solid yellow centerline on a two-lane road indicate?
options: a:Lanes move in opposite directions and drivers are not permitted to pass.,b:Lanes move in opposite directions and drivers may pass when it is safe.,c:Lanes move in the same direction and drivers are not permitted to pass.
note: Double solid yellow lines separate opposing traffic and prohibit passing from either direction.

question: What is the single most effective action to reduce injury or death in a crash?
options: a:Wearing your seat belt.,b:Driving only on weekdays.,c:Staying in the right lane on multilane highways.
note: Wearing a seat belt is the most effective thing you can do to reduce risk of severe injury or death in a crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you have a green light but pedestrians are crossing against a red, you should:
options: a:Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrians.,b:Honk your horn to hurry them.,c:Stop and let the pedestrians cross safely.,d:Drive around them on the shoulder.
note: Yield to pedestrians in the intersection even when you have a green light; safety and the law require yielding to pedestrians.

question: What is the maximum permitted tint (light blockage) for front door windows in Missouri?
options: a:65 percent light blockage.,b:100 percent light blockage.,c:Whatever looks good.
note: Missouri permits tinting on front door windows up to 65 percent light blockage; the rest must remain sufficiently transparent.

question: Who benefits most from wearing seat belts?
options: a:All occupants of a vehicle, including the driver.,b:Only the driver.,c:Only passengers on long trips.
note: Seat belts are most effective when every occupant in the vehicle wears them; unbelted occupants pose a danger to themselves and others in a crash.

question: Before changing lanes on a multilane highway, you should:
options: a:Look in your mirrors and check your blind spot over your shoulder.,b:Sound your horn repeatedly.,c:Turn on your headlights.
note: Check mirrors and glance over your shoulder to verify blind spots are clear before signaling and changing lanes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a No right on red sign mean?
options: a:You may turn right on red if the way is clear.,b:You cannot turn right on red.,c:The intersection has a high number of traffic crashes.
note: When a No right on red sign is posted, right turns on red are prohibited even after a full stop.

question: How old must you be to obtain an instruction permit (young driver)?
options: a:15 years old.,b:14 years old.,c:15 and one-half years old.
note: In Missouri, young drivers may obtain an instruction permit at age 15 to begin supervised driving instruction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is passing prohibited?
options: a:On a hill or curve.,b:When approaching an intersection.,c:When school bus lights are flashing.
note: You must never pass on hills, curves, at intersections, or in other no-passing zones; also never pass a stopped school bus with flashing red lights.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a roadway from a private road or driveway, what should you do?
options: a:Yield to pedestrians and traffic already on the roadway.,b:Blow your horn to warn vehicles you are entering.,c:Stop with part of your car on the roadway to alert other drivers.
note: When entering from a private road or driveway you must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and to vehicles on the roadway.

question: Before backing out of a driveway when children are nearby, you should:
options: a:Walk to the rear of the vehicle to be sure the way is clear.,b:Sound your horn to warn the children.,c:Rev the engine to warn them.,d:Rely only on mirrors while backing slowly.
note: When children are nearby, get out and check behind the vehicle in person; do not rely solely on mirrors.

question: On a highway with double solid yellow center lines, when is crossing allowed?
options: a:Cross only to make a left turn into or from an alley, private road, or driveway.,b:Cross to pass slow vehicles when safe.,c:Never cross under any circumstances.
note: Double solid yellow lines indicate no passing; crossing is permitted only to make a left turn into or from a private road, driveway, or alley.

question: How should you handle driving near a blind pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog?
options: a:Slow down and be prepared to stop.,b:Take the right-of-way immediately.,c:Proceed normally without changing speed.
note: When a blind pedestrian is present, slow down, yield the right-of-way, and be prepared to stop to avoid endangering them.

question: When parallel parking between two vehicles, what should you do first?
options: a:Pull up even with the vehicle in front of the parking space.,b:Turn your wheels to the left immediately.,c:Turn your wheels to the right immediately.
note: After finding a space, signal, check traffic, and stop parallel with the vehicle ahead of the space before beginning the maneuver into the parking spot.

question: Vehicle stopping distances depend on many factors. Which of the following NEVER affects stopping distance?
options: a:Your reaction time.,b:The time of day.,c:The condition of your vehicle's brakes.
note: Stopping distance depends on reaction time, vehicle condition (brakes, tires), vehicle weight, speed, road conditions and visibility—not the time of day itself.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it illegal to drive below the posted speed limit?
options: a:When driving so slowly that you disrupt the normal flow of traffic.,b:When in heavy traffic in a construction zone.,c:Only when driving in rural areas.,d:Whenever there is a police car nearby.
note: Driving so slowly that you impede the normal flow of traffic is illegal and can result in a citation.

question: Anything that requires you to which of the following could cause a crash?
options: a:Take your eyes off the road.,b:Take your hands off the wheel.,c:Take your attention away from the task of driving.
note: Any activity that takes your eyes, hands, or attention away from driving increases crash risk.

question: At a school crossing sign, how should you drive?
options: a:Sound your horn whenever you see children.,b:Watch for children and be prepared to stop.,c:Always stop whether a stop sign is posted or not.
note: Be alert for children at school crossings and be ready to stop; yield to pedestrians in crosswalks.

question: What headlights should you use when driving in rain?
options: a:Use low beam headlights.,b:Use high beam headlights.,c:Use only parking lights.
note: In rain, use low beam headlights to improve visibility and reduce glare for you and other drivers.

question: If sleet or snow begins while you are driving, what should you do?
options: a:Approach all vehicles with caution.,b:Allow extra space between your vehicle and vehicles ahead.,c:Keep windshield and mirrors clear.
note: In snowy or icy conditions increase following distance and keep windows and mirrors clear so you can see and stop safely.

question: Which is true about seat belts and child restraints?
options: a:Never place a rear-facing infant in the front seat of a vehicle with an active passenger airbag.,b:An airbag by itself is always safer than a seat belt.,c:Infants may be held safely by a strong adult during travel.
note: Children 12 and under should ride properly restrained in the rear seat; never place a rear-facing infant restraint where an active passenger airbag is present.

question: What should you do before switching on the ignition?
options: a:Buckle your safety belt and ensure passengers are buckled.,b:Make sure only adult passengers have fastened belts.,c:Buckle only the driver and child passengers.
note: Make it a routine: fasten your belt and ensure all passengers are properly restrained before starting the vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection where you arrive at the same time as a vehicle on your right, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:Speed up to get through first.,b:Yield to the vehicle on your right and proceed when safe.,c:Drive into the intersection and make the other vehicle stop.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection, yield to vehicles on your right. Proceed only when it is safe to do so.

question: Why is night driving generally more difficult than daytime driving?
options: a:It is more likely to rain at night.,b:Visibility is reduced in the dark.,c:Cars overheat more quickly at night.
note: Night driving reduces your field of vision; use proper headlights and drive slowly enough to stop within the distance you can see.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a freeway, if you miss your exit what should you do?
options: a:Make the exit quickly from your current lane.,b:Stop and back up on the shoulder.,c:Continue to the next exit and re-route safely.
note: If you miss your freeway exit, continue to the next exit and find a safe place to re-route—do not stop, back up, or cross medians.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are driving so slowly that traffic is backing up behind you, what should you do?
options: a:Decrease your speed.,b:Pull off the right side of the road and let traffic pass.,c:Not let the other cars pass your vehicle.
note: If your slow driving is holding up traffic on a two-lane road, pull over when safe to let others pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To change lanes safely, what sequence should you follow?
options: a:Signal, check your mirrors, and change lanes.,b:Check your mirrors and signal, then change lanes.,c:Signal, check mirrors, check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move, then change lanes.
note: Signal, check mirrors, look over your shoulder to check the blind spot, and change lanes only when it is safe to do so.

question: Why must you be cautious when passing a bicycle?
options: a:The bicycle always has the right-of-way.,b:Oncoming traffic may not see you pull out to pass the bicycle.,c:You are moving faster than the bicycle.
note: When passing a bicycle, be careful because oncoming vehicles may not see you move out to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A steady green arrow at an intersection means drivers may:
options: a:Turn in the arrow's direction after yielding to vehicles and pedestrians already in the intersection.,b:Ignore the arrow and proceed straight only.,c:Always stop before turning.,d:Turn without yielding to anyone.
note: A green arrow permits the indicated turn; you must still yield to vehicles and pedestrians already in the intersection.

question: What does a solid red arrow displayed by a traffic signal mean?
options: a:Stop; you may not turn in the direction indicated until a green signal appears.,b:Proceed with caution and turn when safe.,c:It has no meaning and should be ignored.
note: A solid red arrow prohibits movement in the arrow's direction until the signal changes to a green arrow or green light.

question: If the driver behind you wants to pass, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to prevent them from passing.,b:Slow down to create space in front of your vehicle so they can pass safely.,c:Maintain the same speed and block the pass.
note: Slow down to make room ahead of your vehicle so the other driver can complete the pass more easily and quickly.

question: Which of the following is NOT true about winter driving?
options: a:Using cruise control in winter conditions is safe.,b:Winter is the most difficult driving season.,c:Checking antifreeze and washer fluid is especially important.
note: Do not use cruise control on snow, rain, fog, or similar hazardous conditions; winter requires extra caution and proper vehicle fluids.

question: If a tire blows out while driving, what should you do first?
options: a:Hold the wheel firmly and steer straight while easing off the gas, then brake gently when under control.,b:Brake hard immediately.,c:Maintain speed and keep steering steady until you reach a pullover spot.
note: When a tire blows, maintain firm steering to keep vehicle straight, ease off the gas, avoid heavy braking until you have control, then slow and pull over safely.

question: When you hear a fire engine siren behind you, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down until it passes you.,b:Drive with your flashers on.,c:Pull over to the side of the road and stop.
note: You must pull to the side of the road and stop to allow emergency vehicles to pass safely.

question: What color are highway destination (exit/distance) signs?
options: a:Red with white letters.,b:Yellow with black letters.,c:Green with white letters.
note: Destination and distance signs on highways use a green background with white lettering or symbols.

question: If your vehicle breaks down on a highway, what precautions should you take?
options: a:Sit in your car and wait for help with hazards off.,b:Signal, move completely off the road if possible, turn on four-way flashers, and raise the hood.,c:Sound your horn at passing motorists.
note: When disabled, get well off the roadway, activate hazard lights, and use the hood or other signals to alert other drivers.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, what is the correct steering action?
options: a:Overcorrect.,b:Turn the steering wheel in the direction of the skid.,c:Turn your steering wheel into oncoming traffic.
note: When a vehicle skids, steer in the direction of the skid until control is regained; avoid overcorrection.

question: If you hear or see an approaching emergency vehicle while on a divided multilane highway, how should you respond?
options: a:Disregard the signal if other lanes are available for the emergency vehicle.,b:Slow down and move to provide a clear path for the emergency vehicle, then stop if necessary.,c:Stop as quickly as possible in your lane.
note: Slow and, if safe, move aside to create room for the emergency vehicle; do not obstruct its path.

question: If you become stranded during a snowstorm, what is the recommended action?
options: a:Get out of the car and walk for help.,b:Lay down in your car and go to sleep.,c:Stay in your vehicle and wait for help while conserving heat.
note: If stranded in a snowstorm stay with your vehicle; you are more likely to be found and it protects you from exposure and hazards outside.

question: What does a single broken yellow centerline indicate on a two-lane road?
options: a:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and passing is not allowed.,b:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and passing is permitted when safe.,c:Lanes are moving in the same direction and passing is not allowed.
note: A broken yellow centerline separates opposite-direction traffic and permits passing when it is safe to do so.

question: When parking uphill next to a curb, how should you set your steering?
options: a:Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.,b:Keep the front tires straight ahead.,c:Keep rear tires against the curb.
note: When parked uphill with a curb, set the parking brake and turn the wheels away from the curb so the vehicle will roll into the curb if it moves.

question: How should a seat belt fit when properly adjusted?
options: a:Loose across the waist.,b:Buckled snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.,c:Hidden beneath the seat for comfort.
note: Lap belts should lie snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen; shoulder belts should lie across your chest for proper protection.

question: In Missouri, an adult (21+) is prohibited from driving with a minimum blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of:
options: a:0.05 percent.,b:0.02 percent.,c:0.08 percent
note: Missouri law makes it illegal for a driver age 21 or older to operate a vehicle with a BAC of 0.08 percent or more.

question: Before entering a roundabout, you must yield to:
options: a:Vehicles and bicyclists already in the roundabout and pedestrians at crosswalks.,b:Only pedestrians in the roundabout.,c:None; proceed immediately.
note: Yield to traffic and bicyclists in the roundabout and watch for pedestrians at the crosswalks before entering.

question: If an oncoming vehicle fails to dim its high beams, where should you glance to avoid glare?
options: a:Look toward the center of the road.,b:Look toward the right side of the road.,c:Look toward either side of the road.
note: When faced with blinding high beams, glance toward the right edge of the roadway to avoid being temporarily blinded.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you must stop at an intersection and there is no stop line or crosswalk, where should you stop?
options: a:At the point nearest the intersecting roadway where you can see traffic without entering it.,b:You are not required to stop.,c:Where you can see at least 200 feet in both directions even if you must enter the intersecting road.
note: If no stop line or crosswalk is present, stop at the nearest point that gives you a view of approaching traffic without entering the intersection.

question: When are roads especially slippery during a rainstorm?
options: a:For the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rainstorm.,b:Only after it has been raining for an hour.,c:The day after it rains.,d:Only when temperatures are below freezing.
note: Pavement can be very slippery in the first 10 to 15 minutes of rain because oil rises to the surface; this is worse in hot weather.

question: Which of the following are effects alcohol can have on you?
options: a:It impairs your thinking ability.,b:It gives you a feeling of false confidence.,c:It slows your reaction time.
note: Alcohol impairs thinking, slows reaction time, and can give a false sense of confidence; all are effects of alcohol on drivers.

question: If the center of the road has a broken yellow line, what does that indicate?
options: a:Traffic flows in opposite directions and passing is permitted when safe.,b:Both lanes travel in the same direction.,c:No passing is allowed.
note: A broken yellow centerline separates opposing traffic and indicates passing is allowed when it is safe to do so.

question: How does alcohol affect driving skills and judgment?
options: a:It helps driving skills but harms judgement.,b:It harms both driving skills and judgment.,c:It has no effect on either.
note: Alcohol impairs reaction time, vision, judgment, and increases risk-taking—reducing the skills needed for safe driving.

question: What is the purpose of regulatory signs?
options: a:They indicate what a driver must or must not do.,b:They mark places of present danger.,c:They are diamond-shaped and yellow or green.
note: Regulatory signs tell drivers the laws and regulations (what must or must not be done) in that area and must be obeyed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you want to turn left but oncoming traffic is heavy while the light is green, what may you do to prepare for the turn?
options: a:Use the next intersection to turn.,b:Wait at the crosswalk for traffic to clear and don’t enter the intersection.,c:Enter and wait in the center of the intersection when the light is green so you can complete the turn when safe.
note: If the light is green you may enter the intersection to wait for a safe gap to complete your left turn, provided you are not blocking traffic and it is safe to do so.

question: What do round traffic signs typically warn drivers about?
options: a:No passing zones.,b:School zones.,c:Upcoming railroad crossings.
note: Round signs are used to warn drivers that a railroad crossing is ahead; use extra caution in these areas.

question: What does a solid yellow line on your side of the centerline indicate?
options: a:Do not pass.,b:Pass with caution.,c:Slow down.
note: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means passing is prohibited from your direction.

question: What is one danger of a leaky exhaust system?
options: a:It can lead to carbon monoxide entering the vehicle.,b:It decreases fuel economy.,c:It makes the engine quieter.
note: An exhaust leak can allow carbon monoxide into the passenger area; fix exhaust leaks promptly to avoid poisoning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When the traffic light turns solid yellow as you approach, what should you do?
options: a:Stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely.,b:Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.,c:Ignore it and proceed at the same speed.
note: A steady yellow warns that the light will turn red; stop if you can do so safely, otherwise proceed through with caution.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a turn or changing lanes, what is required of drivers?
options: a:Signal only if there is visible traffic.,b:Signal only at night.,c:Always signal your intentions.
note: You must always signal when turning, changing lanes, or pulling away from a curb to communicate your intentions to others.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are stopped by a police officer, you should:
options: a:Get out of the vehicle immediately.,b:Unbuckle and walk toward the officer.,c:Stay in your vehicle with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer to approach.,d:Reach for your license and registration before the officer reaches you.
note: Remain in the vehicle, keep your hands visible, and only retrieve documents when the officer requests them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a flashing red traffic light, you must:
options: a:Come to a full stop and proceed only when safe.,b:Slow down and continue without stopping.,c:Yield to traffic on the left only.
note: A flashing red light functions like a stop sign; stop and then proceed when the way is clear.

question: Which of the following does NOT influence Blood Alcohol Content (BAC)?
options: a:Your body weight.,b:How much you drink.,c:The type of alcoholic beverage you drink.
note: BAC depends on amount consumed, time between drinks, and body weight; the type of beverage does not change BAC directly.

question: Which of the following commonly causes traffic accidents?
options: a:Inattentive driving, excessive speed for conditions, and following too closely.,b:Only bad weather.,c:Strictly vehicle defects.
note: Crashes are often caused by driver inattention, speeding for conditions, and following other vehicles too closely; all are common contributors.

question: As alcohol accumulates in your blood, what effects occur?
options: a:Your reactions slow down and you become more confident.,b:Your reaction time improves.,c:It speeds up alcohol metabolism.
note: Alcohol slows reactions, can increase confidence, and causes more errors—reducing driving ability.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a steady yellow arrow indicate?
options: a:Prepare to stop; a red arrow is about to appear.,b:You may turn left after yielding.,c:You should accelerate to clear the intersection.
note: A steady yellow arrow warns that the protected turn is ending and a red arrow will follow; stop if it is safe to do so.

question: Which of the following is not a factor in determining how far it takes to stop your vehicle?
options: a:Steering ability.,b:Braking distance.,c:Reaction distance.,d:Perception time.
note: Stopping distance depends on perception time, reaction distance, and braking distance; steering ability is not a component of the stopping distance calculation.

question: How does consuming alcohol affect a person who then drives?
options: a:Alcohol makes drivers better because they are more careful.,b:Alcohol impairs control over body and mind and reduces ability to operate a vehicle.,c:Drivers are always aware of the risks they are taking.
note: Alcohol is a depressant that impairs judgment, vision, concentration, and reaction time, making driving unsafe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, who must yield?
options: a:The driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.,b:The largest vehicle has the right-of-way.,c:The car on the left has the right-of-way.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection, the vehicle on the left should yield to the vehicle on the right.

question: When driving near heavy trucks you and other highway users must allow for what?
options: a:The decreased stopping distance required by large vehicles.,b:The increased stopping distance required by large vehicles.,c:The decreased noise of larger vehicles.
note: Large trucks require much more distance to stop. Stay out of their blind spots and give them extra space to maneuver and stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a left turn, to whom must you yield the right-of-way?
options: a:Other drivers already in the intersection.,b:Oncoming traffic.,c:Pedestrians already in the intersection.
note: When turning left you must yield to oncoming traffic and also to pedestrians in the intersection or crosswalk.

question: How can stress affect your driving?
options: a:It can reduce your ability to concentrate and drive safely.,b:It decreases the chance of an accident.,c:It causes you to fall asleep at the wheel.
note: Stress and strong emotions can impair judgment and concentration, increasing the risk of poor driving decisions; avoid driving when emotionally unstable.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which traffic light indicates you should slow down and proceed with caution at an intersection?
options: a:A flashing red light.,b:A solid yellow light.,c:A flashing yellow light.
note: A flashing yellow light means slow down, proceed with caution, and be ready to stop if necessary.

question: What do work zone signs indicate?
options: a:Less-than-ideal driving conditions due to road work.,b:It is summer.,c:You must immediately stop and back up.
note: Orange work zone signs warn that people are working on or near the road and that conditions may require extra caution.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
