question: At a four-way stop, if two drivers arrive simultaneously, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver on the left has the right-of-way.,b:The driver on the right has the right-of-way.,c:One driver may continue driving without stopping.
note: When two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, yield to the vehicle on your right.

question: What does a single dashed yellow centerline mean?
options: a:Drivers may pass if it is safe to do so.,b:Both lanes travel in the same direction.,c:Passing is prohibited.
note: A single dashed yellow line separates opposing traffic and permits passing when it is safe and legal to do so.

question: If you see an animal in the roadway, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down and pass the animal slowly to avoid startling it.,b:Honk repeatedly to move the animal quickly.,c:Pass as closely as possible to avoid delays.
note: Exercise caution and slow down; pass animals slowly and give them a wide berth to avoid startling them into unpredictable movements.

question: Guide or destination signs are what color?
options: a:Green,b:Yellow,c:Red
note: Guide signs that indicate directions and distances are green with white letters and symbols.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a steady yellow light, what should you do?
options: a:Slow and stop if you can do so safely; otherwise proceed through the intersection.,b:Accelerate to avoid a red light.,c:Continue as if you have the right-of-way.
note: A steady yellow warns the signal will soon be red; stop if you can safely do so, otherwise proceed with caution.

question: Your vehicle's stopping distance increases when stopping on:
options: a:A wet or icy road.,b:A paved highway in good condition.,c:At night.,d:A downhill grade.
note: Stopping distances grow on wet or icy surfaces, loose gravel, or at higher speeds; allow extra distance in poor conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you use your turn signal?
options: a:Only when changing lanes.,b:When pulling into or out of a parking space and when changing lanes.,c:Only when pulling into traffic from an alley.
note: Always signal when changing lanes, pulling into or out of parking, or pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area to communicate your intentions.

question: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, what is the best response?
options: a:Flash your lights to show you are right.,b:Stay calm and move out of the aggressive driver's way.,c:Call the police immediately from the roadway.
note: If cut off by an aggressive driver, avoid escalating the situation. Stay calm and get out of their way to reduce risk.

question: What is a \No zone\" around a large vehicle?"
options: a:A one-way traffic area.,b:The blind spot areas around large trucks and buses.,c:A designated no passing zone.
note: \No zones\" are the large blind spots around trucks and buses where smaller vehicles may disappear from the driver’s view."

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a posted speed limit represent?
options: a:The maximum or minimum legal speed under ideal conditions.,b:A suggested safe speed regardless of conditions.,c:The speed you must drive even in dangerous conditions.
note: Speed limits indicate the maximum (or minimum) legal speed under ideal conditions; drivers should drive slower when conditions are hazardous.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking uphill where a curb is present, how should you position your front wheels?
options: a:Keep the front wheels straight and set the parking brake.,b:Turn the front wheels toward the curb.,c:Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
note: On an uphill curb, turn the front wheels away from the curb so the vehicle will not roll into traffic if brakes fail.

question: What should be your first response when visibility decreases?
options: a:Turn on your headlights.,b:Turn on your windshield wipers.,c:Reduce your speed.
note: When visibility falls, reduce speed first so you have more time to react to hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should drivers treat a flashing red traffic light?
options: a:Drive through if there is no crossing traffic.,b:Treat it like a stop sign and stop.,c:Continue driving because you have the right-of-way.
note: A flashing red signal functions like a stop sign: come to a complete stop, then proceed when safe.
